sentences.zh: 李適李適，字子至，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Li Shi, courtesy name Zizhi, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, whose courtesy name was Zizi, came from Wannian in the capital district of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，再調猗氏尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was twice appointed magistrate of Yi County.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree and served two terms as magistrate of Yi County.

sentences.zh: 武后修《三教珠英》書，以李嶠、張昌宗為使，取文學士綴集，於是適與王無競、尹元凱、富嘉謨、宋之問、沈佺期、閻朝隱、劉允濟在選。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu compiled the book Pearls of Excellence from the Three Teachings, she appointed Li Jiao and Zhang Changzong as commissioners and gathered literary scholars to compile it. At that time Li Shi was selected together with Wang Wujing, Yin Yuankai, Fu Jiamou, Song Zhiwen, Shen Quanqi, Yan Chaoyin, and Liu Yunji.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu undertook compilation of the Pearls of Excellence from the Three Teachings, appointing Li Jiao and Zhang Changzong as commissioners to gather literary scholars for the work, Li Shi was among those chosen, along with Wang Wujing, Yin Yuankai, Fu Jiamou, Song Zhiwen, Shen Quanqi, Yan Chaoyin, and Liu Yunji.

sentences.zh: 書成，遷戶部員外郎，俄兼脩書學士。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, he was promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Revenue and soon also served as a Scholar of the Book Compilation Institute.
translations.idiomatic: After the work was finished, he was promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Revenue and, before long, was also made a Scholar of the Book Compilation Institute.

sentences.zh: 景龍初，又擢脩文館學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jinglong era, he was again promoted to Scholar of the Hall of Cultivation of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jinglong era, he was promoted once more, this time to Scholar of the Hall of Cultivation of Literature.

sentences.zh: 睿宗時，待詔宣光閣，再選工部侍郎。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Ruizong, he served as a waiting attendant at the Xuanguang Pavilion and was twice selected as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ruizong he served as a waiting attendant at the Xuanguang Pavilion and was twice appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十九，贈貝州刺史。

translations.literal: He died at the age of forty-nine and was posthumously appointed Governor of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-nine and was posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗夢與人論大衍數，寤而曰：「吾壽盡此乎！」

translations.literal: Once he dreamed of discussing the numbers of the Great Expansion with someone, and upon waking said: "Has my lifespan reached its end here!
translations.idiomatic: He once dreamed that he was debating the numerology of the Great Expansion with another man; when he awoke he said, "Surely my allotted years end here!

sentences.zh: 敕其子曰：「霸陵原西視京師，吾樂之，可營墓，樹十松焉。」

translations.literal: He instructed his son: "West of the plain of the Ba Mausoleum, overlooking the capital—that is where I would be happy. You may prepare a tomb there and plant ten pines."
translations.idiomatic: He charged his son: "West of the Ba Mausoleum plateau, where one looks out upon the capital—that is where I would be content. Have a tomb prepared there and plant ten pines."

sentences.zh: 及未病時，衣冠往，寢石榻上，置所撰《九經要句》及素琴於前，士貴其達。

translations.literal: Before he fell ill, he went there dressed in his official robes, lay on a stone couch, and placed his compiled Essential Lines from the Nine Classics and a plain zither before him. Men of quality admired his clarity of mind.
translations.idiomatic: While still in health he went there in full official dress, lay upon a stone couch, and set before him his own compilation, Essential Lines from the Nine Classics, together with an unadorned zither. Men of standing praised his enlightened composure.

sentences.zh: 子 季卿子季卿，亦能文，舉明經、博學宏辭，調鄠尉。

translations.literal: His son Ji Qing was also skilled at writing. He passed the examinations in the Classicist and Broad Learning and Eloquent Prose categories and was appointed magistrate of Hu County.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji Qing was likewise accomplished in letters. He passed the Classicist examination and the Broad Learning and Eloquent Prose examination and was appointed magistrate of Hu County.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，為中書舍人，以累貶通州別駕。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Suzong, he served as Secretariat Drafter and was demoted to Vice-Prefect of Tongzhou on account of accumulated offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Suzong he served as a Secretariat Drafter, but because of repeated offenses was demoted to Vice-Prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，還為京兆少尹，復授舍人，進吏部侍郎、河南江淮宣慰使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong ascended the throne, Ji Qing returned as Vice Magistrate of the capital prefecture, was again appointed Drafter, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel and Commissioner to Pacify Henan and the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong came to the throne, Ji Qing was restored as Vice Magistrate of the capital prefecture, again appointed Drafter, and then promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel and Commissioner to Pacify Henan and the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 振拔幽滯，號振職。

translations.literal: He promoted those hidden and overlooked and was known for revitalizing his office.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted up the neglected and the overlooked, and was known for invigorating the duties of his post.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，終右散騎常侍，遺命以布車一乘葬，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: During the Dali era he ended his career as Right Regular Attendant of the Privy Council, left instructions to be buried with a single cart of cloth, and was posthumously given the title Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali period he ended as Right Regular Attendant of the Privy Council, left orders that he be buried with only one cart of plain cloth, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 季卿在朝，薦進才髦，與人交，有終始，恢博君子也。

translations.literal: While in court, Ji Qing recommended talented men. In his dealings with others he was constant from beginning to end—a broad and generous gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In office Ji Qing recommended men of talent, and in friendship he was steadfast from first to last—a man of expansive learning and true gentlemanly bearing.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗景龍二年，始于脩文館置大學士四員、學士八員，直學士十二員，象四時、八節、十二月。

translations.literal: Initially, in the second year of Jinglong under Emperor Zhongzong, the Hall of Cultivation of Literature first established four Grand Scholars, eight Scholars, and twelve Direct Scholars, symbolizing the four seasons, eight solar terms, and twelve months.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in the second year of Jinglong under Emperor Zhongzong, the Hall of Cultivation of Literature was given four Grand Scholars, eight Scholars, and twelve Direct Scholars, in correspondence with the four seasons, eight solar terms, and twelve months.

sentences.zh: 於是李嶠、宗楚客、趙彥昭、韋嗣立為大學士，適、劉憲、崔湜、鄭愔、盧藏用、李乂、岑羲、劉子玄為學士，薛稷、馬懷素、宋之問、武平一、杜審言、沈佺期、閻朝隱為直學士，又召徐堅、韋元旦、徐彥伯、劉允濟等滿員。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jiao, Zong Chuke, Zhao Yanzhao, and Wei Sili were Grand Scholars; Li Shi, Liu Xian, Cui Shi, Zheng Yin, Lu Zangyong, Li Yi, Cen Xi, and Liu Zixuan were Scholars; Xue Ji, Ma Huaisu, Song Zhiwen, Wu Pingyi, Du Shenyan, Shen Quanqi, and Yan Chaoyin were Direct Scholars. Xu Jian, Wei Yuandian, Xu Yanbo, Liu Yunji, and others were also summoned to fill all the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Li Jiao, Zong Chuke, Zhao Yanzhao, and Wei Sili were made Grand Scholars; Li Shi, Liu Xian, Cui Shi, Zheng Yin, Lu Zangyong, Li Yi, Cen Xi, and Liu Zixuan were made Scholars; and Xue Ji, Ma Huaisu, Song Zhiwen, Wu Pingyi, Du Shenyan, Shen Quanqi, and Yan Chaoyin were made Direct Scholars. Xu Jian, Wei Yuandian, Xu Yanbo, Liu Yunji, and others were also summoned until every post was filled.

sentences.zh: 其後被選者不一。

translations.literal: Thereafter those selected for the posts were not always the same.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the men chosen for these posts varied from time to time.

sentences.zh: 凡天子饗會游豫，唯宰相及學士得從。

translations.literal: Whenever the Son of Heaven held feasts or went on pleasure outings, only the chief ministers and the scholars were permitted to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor held banquets or went on pleasure excursions, only the chief ministers and the scholars of the hall were allowed to follow.

sentences.zh: 春幸梨園，並渭水祓除，則賜細柳圈辟癘；

translations.literal: In spring, when he visited the Pear Orchard and performed the Wei River purification rite, they were given fine willow circlets to ward off pestilence;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, when the court visited the Pear Orchard and performed the Wei River rite of purification, the scholars were granted fine willow circlets to ward off pestilence;

sentences.zh: 夏宴蒲萄園，賜硃櫻；

translations.literal: in summer, at feasts in the Grape Garden, they were given crimson cherries;
translations.idiomatic: in summer, at banquets in the Grape Garden, they received crimson cherries;

sentences.zh: 秋登慈恩浮圖，獻菊花酒稱壽；

translations.literal: in autumn, when he ascended the Ci'en Pagoda, they presented chrysanthemum wine and offered wishes for long life;
translations.idiomatic: in autumn, when the emperor climbed the Ci'en Pagoda, they offered chrysanthemum wine and voiced wishes for his longevity;

sentences.zh: 冬幸新豐，曆白鹿觀，上驪山，賜浴湯池，給香粉蘭澤，從行給翔麟馬，品官黃衣各一。

translations.literal: in winter, when he visited Xinfeng, passed through the Bailu Abbey, and ascended Mount Li, they were granted baths in the hot springs and given fragrant powder and orchid unguents; those who accompanied him were given Xianglin horses, and each attendant of rank received one yellow robe.
translations.idiomatic: in winter, when he visited Xinfeng, passed through the Bailu Abbey, and went up Mount Li, they were granted baths in the hot springs and supplied with fragrant powder and orchid unguents; those in the retinue were given Xianglin horses, and each attendant of rank received a yellow robe.

sentences.zh: 帝有所感即賦詩，學士皆屬和。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor was moved by something he would compose a poem, and the scholars would all write matching verses.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor was stirred to feeling he would compose a poem, and the scholars would all supply matching verses.

sentences.zh: 當時人所歆慕，然皆狎猥佻佞，忘君臣禮法，惟以文華取幸。

translations.literal: At the time people envied them, yet they were all familiar, frivolous, and sycophantic, forgetting the proprieties between ruler and minister and seeking favor solely through literary brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: People of the day envied them, yet they were all overly familiar, frivolous, and obsequious, heedless of the proprieties between ruler and minister and relying on literary brilliance alone to win favor.

sentences.zh: 若韋元旦、劉允濟、沈佺期、宋之問、閻朝隱等無它稱，附篇左雲。

translations.literal: Men such as Wei Yuandian, Liu Yunji, Shen Quanqi, Song Zhiwen, and Yan Chaoyin had no other reputation to speak of; their accounts are appended below.
translations.idiomatic: Figures such as Wei Yuandian, Liu Yunji, Shen Quanqi, Song Zhiwen, and Yan Chaoyin had no other distinction worth noting; their biographies are appended below.

sentences.zh: 韋元旦韋元旦，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Yuandian, a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuandian was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖澄，越王府記室，撰《女誡》傳于時。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wei Cheng served as secretary to the Prince of Yue and compiled the Admonitions for Women, which circulated widely in his day.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wei Cheng had been secretary to the Prince of Yue and wrote the Admonitions for Women, which was widely circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 元旦擢進士第，補東阿尉，遷左台監察御史。

translations.literal: Yuandian passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Dong'e, and was promoted to Investigating Censor of the Left Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandian passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Dong'e, and was then promoted to Investigating Censor of the Left Censorate.

sentences.zh: 與張易之有姻屬，易之敗，貶感義尉。

translations.literal: He was related by marriage to Zhang Yizhi; when Yizhi fell from power, Yuandian was demoted to magistrate of Ganyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was connected by marriage to Zhang Yizhi; when Yizhi was overthrown, Yuandian was demoted to magistrate of Ganyi.

sentences.zh: 俄召為主客員外郎，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites and was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recalled as Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites and was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 舅陸頌妻，韋後弟也，故元旦憑以復進雲。

translations.literal: His wife's mother was Lu Song's wife, who was the younger sister of Empress Wei; therefore Yuandian relied on this connection to regain advancement.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's mother was the wife of Lu Song, who was the younger sister of Empress Wei; thus Yuandian was able to rely on this tie to regain advancement.

sentences.zh: 劉允濟劉允濟，字允濟，河南鞏人，其先出沛國，齊彭城郡丞瓛六世孫。

translations.literal: Liu Yunji, courtesy name Yunji, was a native of Gong in Henan. His ancestors came from Pei Commandery and were sixth-generation descendants of Liu Huan, assistant magistrate of Pengcheng Commandery in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yunji, whose courtesy name was Yunji, came from Gong in Henan. His forebears were descended from Pei Commandery and were sixth-generation descendants of Liu Huan, assistant magistrate of Pengcheng Commandery under Qi.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母尤孝。

translations.literal: He lost his father while young and was especially filial toward his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was especially filial toward his mother.

sentences.zh: 工文辭，與王勃齊名。

translations.literal: He was skilled in literary composition and was as famous as Wang Bo.
translations.idiomatic: He was accomplished in literary composition and was ranked equal in fame with Wang Bo.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，補下邽尉，累遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Xi'gui, and was repeatedly promoted to Assistant Historian.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Xi'gui, and rose by stages to Assistant Historian.

sentences.zh: 采魯哀公後十二世接戰國為《魯後春秋》獻之，遷左史，兼直弘文館。

translations.literal: He compiled the Post-Lu Annals, covering the twelve generations after Duke Ai of Lu down through the Warring States, and presented it to the throne. He was promoted to Left Historian and concurrently served as Direct Attendant of the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the twelve generations after Duke Ai of Lu through the Warring States period, he compiled the Post-Lu Annals and presented it to the throne. He was promoted to Left Historian and concurrently appointed Direct Attendant of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 武后明堂成，奏賦述功德，手詔褒咨，除著作郎。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu's Bright Hall was completed, he submitted a rhapsody describing its merit and virtue. The empress personally issued an edict praising and commending him, and he was appointed Historian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall of Empress Wu was completed, he submitted a rhapsody describing its achievements and virtues. The empress issued a personal edict of praise and commendation, and he was appointed Historian.

sentences.zh: 為來俊臣飛構當死，以母老丐餘年，繫獄，會赦免，貶大庾尉。

translations.literal: Lai Junchen fabricated charges against him for which he should have been put to death. Because his mother was old, he begged to be allowed a few more years of life, was imprisoned, and was spared by a general amnesty, though he was demoted to magistrate of Dayu.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen trumped up charges against him warranting death. Because his mother was aged, he begged to be granted a few remaining years; he was imprisoned, then spared by a general amnesty and demoted to magistrate of Dayu.

sentences.zh: 復為著作佐郎，修國史。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Assistant Historian and worked on the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Assistant Historian and assigned to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「史官善惡必書，使驕主賊臣懼，此權顧輕哉？

translations.literal: He often said: "The duty of the historian is to record good and evil without fail, so that arrogant rulers and treacherous ministers may feel fear. Can this authority be regarded as light?
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "The historian's task is to record good and evil without exception, so that arrogant rulers and treacherous ministers may be afraid. Can such authority be thought slight?

sentences.zh: 而班生受金，陳壽求米，僕乃視如浮雲耳。」

translations.literal: Yet Ban Gu accepted gold and Chen Shou sought rice—I regard such things as floating clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ban Gu took gold and Chen Shou sought rice—as for me, I regard such things as floating clouds.

sentences.zh: 遷鳳閣舍人，坐二張昵狎，除青州長史，有清白稱，巡察使路敬潛言狀。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Drafting Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion, but because of his intimacy with the two Zhangs was removed and appointed Long Administrator of Qingzhou, where he gained a reputation for integrity; the inspection commissioner Lu Jingqian reported his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Drafting Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion, but because of his close association with the two Zhangs was dismissed and appointed Long Administrator of Qingzhou, where he won a reputation for clean conduct; the inspection commissioner Lu Jingqian reported the facts of the case.

sentences.zh: 以內憂去官。

translations.literal: He left office on account of a death in the inner family.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for a close relative.

sentences.zh: 服除，召為修文館學士，既久斥，喜甚，與家人樂飲，數日卒。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended he was summoned as Scholar of the Hall of Cultivation of Literature. Having long been cast out, he was overjoyed; he drank in celebration with his family for several days and then died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was complete he was summoned as Scholar of the Hall of Cultivation of Literature. Long excluded from office, he was overjoyed; he drank in celebration with his family for several days and then died.

sentences.zh: 沈佺期沈佺期，字雲卿，相州內黃人。

translations.literal: Shen Quanqi, courtesy name Yunqing, was a native of Neihuang in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Quanqi, whose courtesy name was Yunqing, came from Neihuang in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，由協律郎累除給事中，考功受賕，劾未究，會張易之敗，遂長流驩州。

translations.literal: After passing the jinshi examination he rose from Director of Harmonization through successive appointments to Secretariat Receptionist. He was under investigation for accepting bribes in the Ministry of Personnel, but before the inquiry was concluded Zhang Yizhi fell from power, and Quanqi was banished far away to Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After earning the jinshi degree he rose from Director of Harmonization through successive posts to Secretariat Receptionist. He was under investigation for taking bribes while serving in the Ministry of Personnel, but before the case was concluded Zhang Yizhi fell, and Quanqi was banished to distant Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 稍遷台州錄事參軍事。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Recording Secretary of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually transferred to Recording Secretary of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 入計，得召見，拜起居郎兼修文館直學士。

translations.literal: When he came to the capital to render accounts he was granted an audience and was appointed Attendant of the Emperor's Movements and Direct Scholar of the Hall of Cultivation of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to the capital to render accounts he was granted an audience and appointed Attendant of the Emperor's Movements and Direct Scholar of the Hall of Cultivation of Literature.

sentences.zh: 既侍宴，帝詔學士等舞《回波》，佺期為弄辭悅帝，還賜牙、緋。

translations.literal: After attending a banquet he was ordered, together with the other scholars, to perform the Returning Waves dance. Quanqi composed playful verses that pleased the emperor, and on his return he was rewarded with ivory and a crimson robe.
translations.idiomatic: Having attended a banquet, he and the other scholars were ordered to perform the Returning Waves dance. Quanqi composed witty verses that delighted the emperor, and upon leaving he was rewarded with ivory and a crimson robe.

sentences.zh: 尋曆中書舍人、太子少詹事。

translations.literal: Before long he successively served as Secretariat Drafter and Junior Chamberlain to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he served in succession as Secretariat Drafter and Junior Chamberlain to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 開元初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the opening of the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 弟全交、全宇，皆有才章而不逮佺期。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Quanjiao and Quanyu were both talented in letters but did not match Quanqi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Quanjiao and Quanyu were both gifted in letters, yet neither equaled Quanqi.

sentences.zh: 宋之問宋之問，字延清，一名少連，汾州人。

translations.literal: Song Zhiwen, courtesy name Yanqing, also called Shaolian, was a native of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhiwen, whose courtesy name was Yanqing and who was also known as Shaolian, came from Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 父令文，高宗時為東臺詳正學士。

translations.literal: His father Song Lingwen served under Emperor Gaozong as Scholar of Detailed Verification of the Eastern Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: His father Song Lingwen served under Emperor Gaozong as Scholar of Detailed Verification of the Eastern Terrace.

sentences.zh: 之問偉儀貌，雄於辯。

translations.literal: Zhiwen had an imposing appearance and was formidable in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen had an imposing bearing and was formidable in debate.

sentences.zh: 甫冠，武后召與楊炯分直習藝館。

translations.literal: Just after coming of age he was summoned by Empress Wu, together with Yang Jiong, to serve on duty at the Hall for Practicing the Arts.
translations.idiomatic: Just after reaching adulthood he was summoned by Empress Wu, together with Yang Jiong, to serve on rotating duty at the Hall for Practicing the Arts.

sentences.zh: 累轉尚方監丞、左奉宸內供奉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Supervisor of the Court of Imperial Manufactories and Inner Attendant of the Left Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Supervisor of the Court of Imperial Manufactories and Inner Attendant of the Left Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武后游洛南龍門，詔從臣賦詩，左史東方蚪詩先成，后賜錦袍，之問俄頃獻，后覽之嗟賞，更奪袍以賜。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu visited Longmen south of the Luo River, she ordered her followers to compose poems. Left Historian Dongfang Diou finished his poem first, and the empress bestowed upon him a brocade robe. In a little while Zhiwen presented his poem; the empress read it, sighed in admiration, took back the robe, and bestowed it upon him instead.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu visited Longmen south of the Luo River, she ordered those accompanying her to compose poems. Left Historian Dongfang Diou finished first, and the empress rewarded him with a brocade robe. Moments later Zhiwen submitted his poem; the empress read it, sighed in admiration, reclaimed the robe, and gave it to him instead.

sentences.zh: 于時張易之等烝昵寵甚，之問與閻朝隱、沈佺期、劉允濟傾心媚附，易之所賦諸篇，盡之問、朝隱所為，至為易之奉溺器。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yizhi and his faction were favored with the utmost intimacy. Zhiwen, together with Yan Chaoyin, Shen Quanqi, and Liu Yunji, devoted themselves wholeheartedly to flattering and attaching themselves to him. All the pieces Yizhi claimed as his own were in fact written by Zhiwen and Chaoyin; Zhiwen even went so far as to hold Yizhi's chamber pot for him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Yizhi and his clique enjoyed the deepest favor. Zhiwen, together with Yan Chaoyin, Shen Quanqi, and Liu Yunji, gave themselves over entirely to fawning attachment. Every piece Yizhi claimed as his own was actually written by Zhiwen and Chaoyin; Zhiwen even served as the bearer of Yizhi's chamber pot.

sentences.zh: 及敗，貶瀧州，朝隱崖州，並參軍事。

translations.literal: When they fell, Zhiwen was demoted to Longzhou and Chaoyin to Yazhou, both as military aides.
translations.idiomatic: When they fell, Zhiwen was demoted to Longzhou and Chaoyin to Yazhou, each as a military aide.

sentences.zh: 之問逃歸洛陽，匿張仲之家。

translations.literal: Zhiwen fled back to Luoyang and hid in the home of Zhang Zhongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen fled back to Luoyang and concealed himself in the home of Zhang Zhongzhi.

sentences.zh: 會武三思復用事，仲之與王同皎謀殺三思安王室，之問得其實，令兄子曇與冉祖雍上急變，因丐贖罪，由是擢鴻臚主簿，天下醜其行。

translations.literal: When Wu Sansi regained power, Zhongzhi and Wang Tongjiao plotted to kill Sansi and secure the royal house. Zhiwen learned the truth of the plot and had his nephew's son Tan, together with Ran Zuyong, submit an urgent report of the conspiracy, thereby begging to redeem his guilt. For this he was promoted to Chief Clerk of the Palace of Imperial Entertainments, though the realm despised his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sansi again came to power, Zhongzhi and Wang Tongjiao plotted to kill Sansi and secure the throne for the imperial house. Zhiwen learned the details and had his brother's son Tan, together with Ran Zuyong, submit an urgent report of the plot, thereby begging remission of his guilt. He was thereupon promoted to Chief Clerk of the Palace of Imperial Entertainments, though the whole realm reviled his behavior.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，遷考功員外郎，諂事太平公主，故見用。

translations.literal: During the Jinglong era he was promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel and curried favor with Princess Taiping; for this reason he was employed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong period he was promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel and fawned upon Princess Taiping; for this reason he was kept in office.

sentences.zh: 及安樂公主權盛，復往諧結，故太平深疾之。

translations.literal: When Princess Anle's power grew great, he went to attach himself to her as well; therefore Princess Taiping deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Anle's influence rose, he went to cultivate ties with her as well; Princess Taiping therefore came to hate him deeply.

sentences.zh: 中宗將用為中書舍人，太平發其知貢舉時賕餉狼藉，下遷汴州長史，未行，改越州長史。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong was about to appoint him Secretariat Drafter, but Princess Taiping exposed the bribery and gifts he had accepted while supervising the examinations. He was demoted to Long Administrator of Bianzhou; before he set out, the appointment was changed to Long Administrator of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong was about to appoint him Secretariat Drafter, but Princess Taiping revealed the bribes and gifts he had accepted while supervising the examinations. He was demoted to Long Administrator of Bianzhou; before he departed, the appointment was changed to Long Administrator of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 頗自力為政。

translations.literal: He exerted himself diligently in governing.
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself diligently to the duties of administration.

sentences.zh: 窮歷剡溪山，置酒賦詩，流布京師，人人傳諷。

translations.literal: He traveled exhaustively through the mountains and streams of Shan, set out wine and composed poems, and when these circulated in the capital everyone recited and admired them.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled thoroughly through the mountains and streams of Shan, held banquets and composed poems, and when these works spread to the capital everyone recited and admired them.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，以獪險盈惡詔流欽州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong came to the throne, an edict banished him to Qinzhou for treacherous, ruthless, and overflowing wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong ascended the throne, an edict exiled him to Qinzhou for treachery, ruthlessness, and overflowing wickedness.

sentences.zh: 祖雍歷中書舍人、刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Ran Zuyong had served as Secretariat Drafter and Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Zuyong had served as Secretariat Drafter and Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 倡飲省中，為御史劾奏，貶蘄州刺史。

translations.literal: He was caught drinking in the offices of the Secretariat and was impeached by the censorate; he was demoted to Prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was discovered drinking in the offices of the Secretariat and was impeached by the censorate; he was demoted to Prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 至是，亦流嶺南，並賜死桂州。

translations.literal: At this time he too was exiled to Lingnan, and both men were ordered to die at Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he too was exiled to Lingnan, and both men were ordered to die at Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 之問得詔震汗，東西步，不引決。

translations.literal: When Zhiwen received the edict he broke out in a cold sweat and paced back and forth, but would not take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhiwen received the edict he broke into a cold sweat and paced east and west, but would not kill himself.

sentences.zh: 祖雍請使者曰：「之問有妻子，幸聽訣。」

translations.literal: Ran Zuyong asked the envoy: "Zhiwen has wife and children; please allow him to take leave of them.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Zuyong asked the envoy, "Zhiwen has a wife and children; please permit him to bid them farewell.

sentences.zh: 使者許之，而之問荒悸不能處家事。

translations.literal: The envoy agreed, but Zhiwen, in panic and confusion, was unable to attend to his household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy consented, but Zhiwen, distraught and bewildered, was unable to put his household affairs in order.

sentences.zh: 祖雍怒曰：「與公俱負國家當死，奈何遲回邪？」

translations.literal: Ran Zuyong angrily said: "You and I have both betrayed the state and ought to die—why hesitate?
translations.idiomatic: Ran Zuyong said in anger, "You and I have both betrayed the state and ought to die—why do you linger?

sentences.zh: 乃飲食洗沐就死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ate, washed himself, and went to his death.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ate, washed himself, and went to meet death.

sentences.zh: 祖雍，江夏王道宗甥，及進士第，有名于時。

translations.literal: Ran Zuyong was a nephew of Prince Dao of Jiangxia. After passing the jinshi examination he was famous in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Zuyong was a nephew of Prince Dao of Jiangxia. After passing the jinshi examination he was renowned in his day.

sentences.zh: 魏建安後迄江左，詩律屢變，至沈約、庾信，以音韻相婉附，屬對精密。

translations.literal: From the Wei and Jian'an periods down through the Eastern Jin, the forms of regulated verse changed repeatedly. By the time of Shen Yue and Yu Xin, tonal harmony was used to lend grace, and parallel phrasing was wrought with precision.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei and Jian'an periods down through the Eastern Jin, poetic forms changed again and again. With Shen Yue and Yu Xin, tonal harmony lent grace and parallel phrasing was wrought with precision.

sentences.zh: 及之問、沈佺期，又加靡麗，回忌聲病，約句准篇，如錦繡成文，學者宗之，號為「沈宋」。

translations.literal: When Zhiwen and Shen Quanqi came afterward, they added further ornate elegance, guarded against tonal faults, and fixed lines to regulated stanzas, like brocade woven into pattern. Scholars took them as models and called them the "Shen-Song" school.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen and Shen Quanqi then added further ornate elegance, guarded against tonal faults, and fixed lines to regulated stanzas, like brocade woven into pattern. Scholars took them as models and called them the "Shen-Song" school.

sentences.zh: 語曰「蘇李居前，沈宋比肩」，謂蘇武、李陵也。

translations.literal: A saying runs, "Su and Li in front, Shen and Song shoulder to shoulder," referring to Su Wu and Li Ling.
translations.idiomatic: People said, "Su and Li lead the way; Shen and Song stand shoulder to shoulder"—meaning Su Wu and Li Ling.

sentences.zh: 初，之問父令文，富文辭，且工書，有力絕人，世稱「三絕」。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhiwen's father Song Lingwen was rich in literary skill and also excelled at calligraphy; his strength surpassed other men, and the age called these his "three supreme talents."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhiwen's father Song Lingwen was rich in literary skill and also excelled at calligraphy; his strength surpassed other men, and his age called these his "three supreme talents."

sentences.zh: 都下有牛善觸，人莫敢嬰，令文直往拔取角，折其頸殺之。

translations.literal: In the capital there was an ox skilled at goring; no one dared approach it. Lingwen went straight up, pulled out its horn, broke its neck, and killed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital there was an ox skilled at goring, and no one dared go near it. Lingwen went straight up, seized its horn, broke its neck, and killed it.

sentences.zh: 既之問以文章起，其弟之悌以蹻勇聞，之愻精草隸，世謂皆得父一絕。

translations.literal: After Zhiwen rose through literary accomplishment, his younger brother Zhitie became known for leaping valor, and Zhisun mastered cursive and clerical script. The world said that each had inherited one of the father's supreme talents.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhiwen rose through literary accomplishment, his younger brother Zhitie became known for leaping valor, and Zhisun mastered cursive and clerical script. People said that each had inherited one of the father's supreme talents.

sentences.zh: 之悌，長八尺。

translations.literal: Zhitie stood eight feet tall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitie stood eight feet in height.

sentences.zh: 開元中，歷劍南節度使、太原尹。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era he successively served as Military Commissioner of Jiannan and Intendant of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era he served in succession as Military Commissioner of Jiannan and Intendant of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 嘗坐事流硃鳶，會蠻陷驩州，授總管擊之。

translations.literal: Once, on account of an offense, he was banished to Zhuyuan. When the barbarians captured Huanzhou he was appointed overall commander to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Once, because of an offense, he was banished to Zhuyuan. When the barbarians captured Huanzhou he was appointed overall commander to strike them.

sentences.zh: 募壯士八人，被重甲，大呼薄賊曰：「獠動即死！」

translations.literal: He recruited eight stalwart men, clad them in heavy armor, and shouted as they closed on the enemy: "Move and you die!
translations.idiomatic: He recruited eight stalwart men, clad them in heavy armor, and shouted as they pressed close upon the enemy, "Move and you die!

sentences.zh: 賊七百人皆伏不能興，遂平賊。

translations.literal: The seven hundred enemy soldiers all prostrated themselves and could not rise; thus the bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred of the enemy prostrated themselves and could not rise; the bandits were thereupon pacified.

sentences.zh: 之愻為連州參軍，刺史聞其善歌，使教婢，日執笏立簾外，唱吟自如。

translations.literal: Zhisun served as military aide of Lianzhou. The prefect, hearing that he sang well, had him teach a maid; each day he stood outside the curtain holding his tablet, chanting and reciting as though at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhisun served as military aide of Lianzhou. The prefect, hearing that he sang well, had him instruct a maid; each day he stood outside the curtain holding his tablet, chanting and reciting with perfect ease.

sentences.zh: 閻朝隱閻朝隱，字友倩，趙州欒城人，少與兄鏡幾、弟仙舟皆著名。

translations.literal: Yan Chaoyin, courtesy name Youqian, was a native of Luancheng in Zhao. In youth he and his elder brother Jingji and younger brother Xianzhou were all renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Chaoyin, whose courtesy name was Youqian, came from Luancheng in Zhao. In youth he and his elder brother Jingji and younger brother Xianzhou were all celebrated.

sentences.zh: 連中進士、孝悌廉讓科，補陽武尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and the Filial Piety, Integrity, and Forbearance examination and was appointed magistrate of Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and the Filial Piety, Integrity, and Forbearance examination and was appointed magistrate of Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 中宗為太子，朝隱以舍人幸。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was crown prince, Chaoyin enjoyed favor as a Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was crown prince, Chaoyin enjoyed favor as a Drafter.

sentences.zh: 性滑稽，屬辭奇詭，為武后所賞。

translations.literal: His nature was comically witty, and his phrasing was strange and bizarre; Empress Wu admired him for this.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was comically witty, and his phrasing was strange and bizarre; Empress Wu admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中、仗內供奉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Receptionist and Inner Attendant within the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to Secretariat Receptionist and Inner Attendant within the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 后有疾，令往禱少室山，乃沐浴，伏身俎盤為犧，請代后疾。

translations.literal: When the empress fell ill she sent him to pray at Mount Shaoshi. He bathed himself, lay prostrate upon the offering tray as a sacrificial victim, and asked to take the empress's illness upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress fell ill she sent him to pray at Mount Shaoshi. He bathed himself, lay prostrate upon the offering tray as a sacrificial victim, and begged to take the empress's illness upon himself.

sentences.zh: 還奏，會后亦愈，大見褒賜。

translations.literal: When he returned and reported, the empress had also recovered; she greatly praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned and made his report, the empress had likewise recovered; she praised and rewarded him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 其資佞諂如此。

translations.literal: Such was the sycophantic character of his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the sycophantic bent of his gifts.

sentences.zh: 景龍初，自崖州遇赦還，累遷著作郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jinglong he returned from Yazhou upon receiving a pardon and was repeatedly promoted to Historian.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Jinglong he returned from Yazhou under a general pardon and rose by stages to Historian.

sentences.zh: 先天中，為秘書少監，坐事貶通州別駕，卒。

translations.literal: During the Xiantian era he served as Vice Director of the Secretariat; because of an offense he was demoted to Bieda of Tongzhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantian era he served as Vice Director of the Secretariat. After an offense he was demoted to Bieda of Tongzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 尹元凱尹元凱，瀛州樂壽人。

translations.literal: Yin Yuankai, courtesy name Yuankai, was a native of Leshou in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yuankai, whose courtesy name was Yuankai, came from Leshou in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 由慈州司倉參軍坐事免，棲遲不出者三十年。

translations.literal: Starting from his post as Army Supervision Officer of Cizhou, he was dismissed because of an offense and lived in seclusion without going out for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as Army Supervision Officer of Cizhou he was dismissed for an offense and lived in seclusion without emerging for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 與張說、盧藏用厚，詔起為右補闕。

translations.literal: He was on close terms with Zhang Yue and Lu Zangyong; by imperial edict he was summoned and appointed Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: On close terms with Zhang Yue and Lu Zangyong, he was summoned by imperial edict and appointed Right Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 時又有富嘉謨、吳少微，皆知名。

translations.literal: At that time there were also Fu Jiamou and Wu Shaowei, both of whom were well known.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fu Jiamou and Wu Shaowei were also celebrated figures.

sentences.zh: 附 富嘉謨 吳少微嘉謨，武功人，舉進士。

translations.literal: Appended biographies: Fu Jiamou and Wu Shaowei. Jiamou was a native of Wugong and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Appended accounts: Fu Jiamou and Wu Shaowei. Jiamou came from Wugong and earned his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 長安中，累轉晉陽尉；

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era he was repeatedly transferred and became Assistant Magistrate of Jinyang;
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he rose by stages to Assistant Magistrate of Jinyang;

sentences.zh: 少微，新安人，亦尉晉陽，尤相友善；

translations.literal: Shaowei was a native of Xin'an and also served as magistrate of Jinyang; the two were especially close friends;
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei came from Xin'an and likewise served as magistrate of Jinyang; the two were especially close friends;

sentences.zh: 有魏穀倚者，為太原主簿，並負文辭，時稱「北京三傑」。

translations.literal: There was also Wei Guyi, who served as Recorder of Taiyuan; all three were renowned for literary talent and were called the Three Outstanding Men of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wei Guyi, Recorder of Taiyuan. All three were celebrated for their writing and were known as the Three Outstanding Men of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 天下文章尚徐、庾，浮俚不競，獨嘉謨、少微本經術，雅厚雄邁，人爭慕之，號「吳富體」。

translations.literal: Writers throughout the realm favored the styles of Xu and Yu, which were frivolous and vulgar and not worth competing with; only Jiamou and Shaowei, grounded in classical learning, wrote in an elegant, substantial, and bold style. People vied to emulate them, and their manner was called the Wu-Fu style.
translations.idiomatic: Writers across the realm still favored the styles of Xu Ling and Yu Xin—light, vulgar work hardly worth emulating—whereas Jiamou and Shaowei, grounded in classical learning, wrote in an elegant, weighty, and bold manner. People rushed to imitate them, and their style was known as the Wu-Fu manner.

sentences.zh: 豫修《三教珠英》。

translations.literal: They took part in compiling Pearls of Excellence from the Three Teachings.
translations.idiomatic: They participated in compiling Pearls of Excellence from the Three Teachings.

sentences.zh: 韋嗣立薦嘉謨、少微並為左台監察御史。

translations.literal: Wei Sili recommended Jiamou and Shaowei, and both were appointed Censors of the Left Office.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sili recommended Jiamou and Shaowei, and both were made Censors of the Left Office.

sentences.zh: 已而嘉謨死，少微方病，聞之為慟，亦卒。

translations.literal: Before long Jiamou died. Shaowei was then ill; when he heard of it he was stricken with grief and also died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jiamou died. Shaowei was already ill; when he heard the news he was overcome with grief and died as well.

sentences.zh: 劉憲劉憲，字元度，宋州寧陵人。

translations.literal: Liu Xian, courtesy name Yuandu, was a native of Ningling in Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian, whose courtesy name was Yuandu, came from Ningling in Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 父思立，在高宗時為名御史。

translations.literal: His father Sili was a celebrated censor during the reign of Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sili was a celebrated censor under Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 于時河南、北大旱，詔遣御史中丞崔謐等分道賑贍，思立建言：「蠶務未畢而遣使撫巡，所至不能無勞餞。

translations.literal: At that time Henan and the north suffered a great drought. An edict dispatched Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Mi and others by separate routes to provide relief. Sili submitted a proposal: "If envoys are sent out on inspection tours before silkworm duties are finished, wherever they arrive there cannot fail to be labor and entertainment expenses.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Henan and the northern regions were stricken by severe drought. The court ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Mi and others to travel separate routes and provide relief. Sili submitted a proposal: "If inspection envoys are dispatched before silkworm work is finished, every place they reach will require labor and hospitality expenses.

sentences.zh: 又賑給須立簿最，稽出入，往返停滯，妨廢且廣。

translations.literal: Moreover, relief distribution requires keeping ledgers and records, checking receipts and expenditures, and the back-and-forth delays cause obstruction and waste on a broad scale.
translations.idiomatic: Relief distribution also requires ledgers and tallies, checking receipts and expenditures, and the delays of travel back and forth will cause widespread disruption and waste.

sentences.zh: 若無驛處，馬須豫集，以一馬勞數家，今農事待雨興作，輟日役，破歲計，本欲安存，更煩擾之。

translations.literal: Where there are no relay stations, horses must be gathered in advance, and one horse will burden several households. Now farm work waits for rain to begin; to suspend daily labor and ruin the year's plan is to add further trouble when the aim was to preserve the people.
translations.idiomatic: Where there are no relay stations, horses must be assembled in advance, and a single horse will burden several households. Farm work now waits on the rains; to suspend daily labor and wreck the year's plans is to add fresh hardship when the goal was to keep people alive.

sentences.zh: 望且責州縣給貸，須秋遣使便。」

translations.literal: I hope that for the time being the prefectures and counties may be ordered to provide loans, and that envoys be sent out only in autumn, when it will be convenient."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that for now the prefectures and counties be ordered to extend loans, and that envoys be sent only in autumn, when travel will be easier."

sentences.zh: 詔聽，罷謐等行。

translations.literal: The edict approved this, and Mi's mission and the others were canceled.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the proposal, and the missions of Mi and the others were called off.

sentences.zh: 遷考功員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Director in the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant Director in the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 始議加明經帖、進士雜文。

translations.literal: He was the first to propose adding written examination papers for the Mingjing degree and miscellaneous compositions for the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He was the first to propose adding written papers to the Mingjing examination and literary compositions to the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 卒官下。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while still in office.

sentences.zh: 憲擢進士，調河南尉，累進左臺監察御史。

translations.literal: Xian passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Henan, and was repeatedly promoted to Censor of the Left Office.
translations.idiomatic: Xian earned his jinshi degree, was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Henan, and rose by stages to Censor of the Left Office.

sentences.zh: 天授中，奉詔按來俊臣罪，憲疾其酷，欲痛繩之，反爲所構，貶潾水令。

translations.literal: During the Tianshou era he was ordered by edict to investigate Lai Junchen's crimes. Xian detested his cruelty and wished to punish him severely, but was instead framed by him and demoted to Magistrate of Linshui.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era he was ordered to investigate Lai Junchen's crimes. Xian loathed the man's cruelty and meant to punish him severely, but was instead framed by him and demoted to Magistrate of Linshui.

sentences.zh: 俊臣死，召為給事中，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: After Junchen died, Xian was summoned as Secretariat Receptionist and then transferred to Drafting Officer at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Junchen's death he was recalled as Secretariat Receptionist and then promoted to Drafting Officer at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 坐善張易之，出為渝州刺史。

translations.literal: Because of his association with Zhang Yizhi, he was sent out as Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For associating with Zhang Yizhi he was sent out as Governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 除太僕少卿，脩國史，兼脩文館學士，遷太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of the Stud, compiled the national history, and concurrently served as Scholar of the Hall of Cultivation of Literature; he was then promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of the Stud, put in charge of compiling the national history, and made a concurrent Scholar of the Hall of Cultivation of Literature before being promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時玄宗在東宮，雅意墳史，憲啟曰：「殿下位副君，有絕人之才，非以尋擿章句，要通大意而已。

translations.literal: At that time Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace and had a deep interest in the classics and histories. Xian submitted a memorial saying: "Your Highness stands as heir to the throne and possesses surpassing talent; the aim is not to hunt through clauses and sentences, but to grasp the larger meaning.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace and devoted himself to the classics and histories. Xian submitted a memorial saying, "Your Highness stands as heir to the throne and possesses surpassing talent; the point is not to pick over clauses and sentences, but to grasp the larger meaning.

sentences.zh: 侍讀褚無量經明行脩，耆年宿望，宜數召問以察其言。」

translations.literal: Your Reader Chu Wuliang is thoroughly versed in the classics and upright in conduct, a man of advanced years and established reputation; he should be summoned frequently and questioned so that his words may be tested."
translations.idiomatic: Your Reader Chu Wuliang is thoroughly versed in the classics and upright in conduct, a man of advanced years and established reputation; he should be summoned often and questioned so that his counsel may be weighed."

sentences.zh: 太子順納。

translations.literal: The crown prince readily accepted this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince readily accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 會卒，贈兗州都督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died and was posthumously appointed Military Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward and was posthumously enfeoffed as Military Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 武后時，敕吏部糊名考判，求高才，惟憲與王適、司馬鍠、梁載言入第二等。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's reign the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to conduct sealed-name examinations and judgments to seek men of high talent; only Xian, Wang Shi, Sima Huang, and Liang Zaiyan entered the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's reign the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to conduct sealed-name examinations and judgments in search of outstanding talent; only Xian, Wang Shi, Sima Huang, and Liang Zaiyan were placed in the second rank.

sentences.zh: 適，幽州人，終雍州司功參軍。

translations.literal: Shi was a native of Youzhou and ended his career as Army Supervision Officer of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi came from Youzhou and ended his career as Army Supervision Officer of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 鍠，河南人，神龍初，以中書侍郎卒。

translations.literal: Huang was a native of Henan; at the beginning of the Shenlong era he died while serving as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Huang came from Henan and died at the opening of the Shenlong era while serving as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 事繼母孝，奉祿不入私舍。

translations.literal: He was filial toward his stepmother and did not keep his salary in his private quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial toward his stepmother and never kept his official salary for private use.

sentences.zh: 與弟銓、伯父希象皆歷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He, his younger brother Quan, and his uncle Xixiang all served as Palace Censors.
translations.idiomatic: He, his younger brother Quan, and his uncle Xixiang all held posts as Palace Censors.

sentences.zh: 希象，剛直不諂，終主爵員外郎。

translations.literal: Xixiang was upright and unflattering and ended his career as Assistant Director of the Bureau of Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Xixiang was upright and would not flatter; he ended his career as Assistant Director of the Bureau of Enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 載言，聊城人，歷鳳閣舍人，專知制誥，終懷州刺史。

translations.literal: Zaiyan was a native of Liaocheng; he served as Drafting Officer of the Phoenix Pavilion, was put in charge of imperial edicts, and ended his career as Governor of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyan came from Liaocheng, served as Drafting Officer of the Phoenix Pavilion and was put in charge of imperial edicts, and ended his career as Governor of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 李邕李邕，字泰和，揚州江都人。

translations.literal: Li Yong, courtesy name Taihe, was a native of Jiangdu in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong, whose courtesy name was Taihe, came from Jiangdu in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父善，有雅行，淹貫古今，不能屬辭，故人號「書簏」。

translations.literal: His father Shan had refined conduct and was thoroughly versed in matters ancient and modern, but could not compose prose; therefore people called him the Book Cabinet.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shan was a man of refined conduct, thoroughly versed in matters ancient and modern, but unable to compose prose; people therefore called him the Book Cabinet.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，累擢崇賢館直學士兼沛王侍讀。

translations.literal: During the Xianqing era he was repeatedly promoted to Direct Scholar of the Chongxian Hall and concurrently served as Reader to the Prince of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianqing era he rose by stages to Direct Scholar of the Chongxian Hall and concurrently served as Reader to the Prince of Pei.

sentences.zh: 為《文選注》，敷析淵洽，表上之，賜賚頗渥。

translations.literal: He wrote a Commentary on Selections of Refined Literature, explaining its passages with deep and thorough learning, submitted it to the throne, and received lavish gifts in return.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a Commentary on Selections of Refined Literature, explaining its passages with deep and thorough learning, presented it to the throne, and received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 除潞王府記室參軍，為涇城令，坐與賀蘭敏之善，流姚州，遇赦還。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretary of the Prince of Lu's household and served as Magistrate of Jingcheng; because of his association with Helan Minzhi he was exiled to Yaozhou, but returned upon receiving a pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretary of the Prince of Lu's household and served as Magistrate of Jingcheng. For associating with Helan Minzhi he was exiled to Yaozhou, but returned under a general pardon.

sentences.zh: 居汴、鄭間講授，諸生四遠至，傳其業，號「《文選》學」。

translations.literal: He lived between Bian and Zheng and lectured there; students came from the four quarters, transmitted his learning, and it was called Wenxuan Studies.
translations.idiomatic: He lived between Bian and Zheng and lectured there. Students came from far and wide to carry on his teaching, which came to be known as Wenxuan Studies.

sentences.zh: 邕少知名。

translations.literal: Yong was famous from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was celebrated from youth.

sentences.zh: 始善注《文選》，釋事而忘意。

translations.literal: At first Shan annotated Selections of Refined Literature by explaining the facts but forgetting the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shan annotated Selections of Refined Literature by explaining the facts while missing the meaning.

sentences.zh: 書成以問邕，邕不敢對，善詰之，邕意欲有所更，善曰：「試為我補益之。」

translations.literal: When the book was finished he asked Yong about it. Yong did not dare reply. Shan pressed him, and Yong intended to make changes. Shan said: "Try to supplement and improve it for me."
translations.idiomatic: When the book was finished he asked Yong to review it. Yong did not dare answer. Shan pressed him, and Yong meant to make changes. Shan said, "Then try to supplement and improve it for me."

sentences.zh: 邕附事見義，善以其不可奪，故兩書並行。

translations.literal: Yong added explanations of the facts to bring out the meaning. Shan, seeing that his work could not be displaced, therefore let both books circulate together.
translations.idiomatic: Yong added explanations that brought out the meaning behind the facts. Shan, seeing that his own work could not be displaced, let both books circulate side by side.

sentences.zh: 既冠，見特進李嶠，自言「讀書未遍，願一見秘書」。

translations.literal: After coming of age he visited Li Jiao, who held the honorary title of Special Advancement, and said of himself: "I have not yet read widely and wish to see the books of the Secretariat once."
translations.idiomatic: After coming of age he visited Li Jiao, who held the honorary title of Special Advancement, and said, "I have not yet read widely enough and wish to spend time among the books of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「秘閣萬卷，豈時日能習邪？」

translations.literal: Jiao said: "The Secret Archive holds ten thousand scrolls—how could they be mastered in a short time?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiao said, "The Secret Archive holds ten thousand scrolls—how could they be mastered in a short time?"

sentences.zh: 邕固請，乃假直秘書。

translations.literal: Yong pressed his request, and Jiao therefore lent him temporary access to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yong pressed his request, and Jiao finally lent him temporary access to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾辭去，嶠驚，試問奧篇隱帙，了辯如響。

translations.literal: Before long he took leave to depart. Jiao was astonished and tested him with abstruse texts and hidden volumes; Yong answered with perfect clarity, as if echoing the books themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took his leave. Jiao was astonished and tested him with abstruse texts and hidden volumes; Yong answered with perfect clarity, as if the books themselves were speaking.

sentences.zh: 嶠歎曰：「子且名家！」

translations.literal: Jiao sighed and said: "You will surely become a master!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiao sighed and said, "You will surely become a master!"

sentences.zh: 嶠為內史，與監察御史張廷珪薦邕文高氣方直，才任諫諍，乃召拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: When Jiao served as Director of the Secretariat, he and Censor Zhang Tinggui recommended Yong for the loftiness of his writing, the squareness and uprightness of his character, and his fitness for remonstrance; he was then summoned and appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiao served as Director of the Secretariat, he and Censor Zhang Tinggui recommended Yong for the loftiness of his writing, the squareness and uprightness of his character, and his fitness for remonstrance; he was summoned and appointed Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞宋璟劾張昌宗等反狀，武后不應，邕立階下大言曰：「璟所陳社稷大計，陛下當聽。」

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Song Jing impeached Zhang Changzong and others for treason, but Empress Wu did not respond. Yong stood below the steps and spoke loudly: "What Jing has presented concerns the great plan of the state; Your Majesty should listen."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Song Jing impeached Zhang Changzong and others for treason, but Empress Wu did not respond. Yong stood below the steps and cried out, "What Jing has presented concerns the great plan of the state; Your Majesty should listen."

sentences.zh: 后色解，即可璟奏。

translations.literal: The empress's expression softened, and she immediately approved Jing's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's expression softened, and she immediately approved Jing's memorial.

sentences.zh: 邕出，或讓曰：「子位卑，一忤旨，禍不測。」

translations.literal: When Yong went out, someone reproached him, saying: "Your rank is low; one offense against the throne and disaster is unforeseeable."
translations.idiomatic: When Yong left, someone reproached him, saying, "Your rank is low; one offense against the throne and disaster is unforeseeable."

sentences.zh: 邕曰：「不如是，名亦不傳。」

translations.literal: Yong said: "If I had not done so, my name would not be handed down either."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "If I had not done so, my name would not be handed down either."

sentences.zh: 中宗立，鄭普思以方技幸，擢秘書監。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong ascended the throne, Zheng Pusi won favor through occult arts and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong ascended the throne, Zheng Pusi won favor through occult arts and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 邕諫曰：「陛下躬政日淺，有九重之嚴，未聞道路橫議。

translations.literal: Yong remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty has personally governed for only a short time, and within the ninefold palaces there is solemn dignity; one does not yet hear reckless talk in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Yong remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty has personally governed for only a short time, and within the ninefold palaces there is solemn dignity; one does not yet hear reckless talk in the streets.

sentences.zh: 今籍籍皆言普思馮詭惑，說妖祥，陛下不知，猥見驅使。

translations.literal: Now everywhere people are saying that Pusi relies on deceit and delusion, preaching omens and portents, yet Your Majesty, unaware of this, has demeaned yourself by employing him.
translations.idiomatic: Now everywhere people are saying that Pusi relies on deceit and delusion, preaching omens and portents, yet Your Majesty, unaware of this, has demeaned yourself by employing him.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『《詩》三百，一言以蔽之，曰：思無邪。』

translations.literal: Confucius said: "The three hundred pieces of the Book of Poetry may be summed up in one phrase: Have no depraved thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "The three hundred pieces of the Book of Poetry may be summed up in one phrase: Have no depraved thoughts.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠以普思術可致長生，則爽鳩氏且因之永有天下，非陛下乃今可得；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly believes Pusi's arts can bring long life, then Lord Shuangjiao would long ago have possessed the realm forever through them, and it would not be Your Majesty who holds it today;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly believes Pusi's arts can bring long life, then Lord Shuangjiao would long ago have possessed the realm forever through them, and it would not be Your Majesty who holds it today;

sentences.zh: 能致神人邪，秦、漢且因之永有天下，非陛下乃今可得；

translations.literal: if they could summon divine beings, then Qin and Han would long ago have possessed the realm forever through them, and it would not be Your Majesty who holds it today;
translations.idiomatic: if they could summon divine beings, then Qin and Han would long ago have possessed the realm forever through them, and it would not be Your Majesty who holds it today;

sentences.zh: 能致佛法邪，梁武帝且因之永有天下，非陛下乃今可得；

translations.literal: if they could summon the power of Buddhism, then Emperor Wu of Liang would long ago have possessed the realm forever through it, and it would not be Your Majesty who holds it today;
translations.idiomatic: if they could summon the power of Buddhism, then Emperor Wu of Liang would long ago have possessed the realm forever through it, and it would not be Your Majesty who holds it today;

sentences.zh: 能鬼道邪，墨翟、干寶且各獻其主，永有天下，非陛下乃今可得。

translations.literal: if they could summon the way of ghosts, then Mozi and Gan Bao would each have offered them to their lords and possessed the realm forever, and it would not be Your Majesty who holds it today.
translations.idiomatic: if they could summon the way of ghosts, then Mozi and Gan Bao would each have offered them to their lords and possessed the realm forever, and it would not be Your Majesty who holds it today.

sentences.zh: 自古堯、舜稱聖者，臣觀所以行，皆在人事，敦睦九族，平章百姓，不聞以鬼神道治天下，惟陛下省察。」

translations.literal: From antiquity the men called sage rulers, such as Yao and Shun, governed, as I observe, entirely through human affairs—making the nine clans harmonious and giving proper weight to the common people. I have never heard of ruling the realm by the way of ghosts and spirits. I ask only that Your Majesty reflect on this."
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity the men called sage rulers, such as Yao and Shun, governed, as I observe, entirely through human affairs—making the nine clans harmonious and giving proper weight to the common people. I have never heard of ruling the realm by the way of ghosts and spirits. I ask only that Your Majesty reflect on this."

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: The advice was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The advice was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 五王誅，坐善張柬之，出為南和令，貶富州司戶參軍事。

translations.literal: When the Five Princes were executed, Yong was punished for his association with Zhang Jianzhi; he was sent out as Magistrate of Nanhe and demoted to Army Supervision Officer of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Five Princes were executed, Yong was punished for associating with Zhang Jianzhi; he was sent out as Magistrate of Nanhe and demoted to Army Supervision Officer of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 韋氏平，召拜左臺殿中侍御史，彈劾任職，人頗憚之。

translations.literal: After the Wei clan was suppressed, he was summoned and appointed Palace Censor of the Left Office; he performed impeachments conscientiously, and people greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei clan was suppressed, he was summoned and appointed Palace Censor of the Left Office. He performed his impeachments conscientiously, and people greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 譙王重福謀反，邕與洛州司馬崔日知捕支黨，遷戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Prince Qiao Chongfu plotted rebellion, Yong and Luozhou Assistant Governor Cui Rizhi captured his followers; he was then promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qiao Chongfu plotted rebellion, Yong and Luozhou Assistant Governor Cui Rizhi captured his followers, and Yong was promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 岑羲、崔湜惡日用，而邕與之交，玄宗在東宮，邕及崔隱甫、倪若水同被禮遇，羲等忌之，貶邕舍城丞。

translations.literal: Cen Xi and Cui Shi hated Cui Riyong, but Yong associated with him. When Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace, Yong, together with Cui Yinpu and Ni Ruoshui, was all treated with honor; Cen and the others resented this and demoted Yong to Assistant Magistrate of Shecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Xi and Cui Shi hated Cui Riyong, but Yong associated with him. When Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace, Yong, together with Cui Yinpu and Ni Ruoshui, all enjoyed favored treatment; Cen and the others resented this and demoted Yong to Assistant Magistrate of Shecheng.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，召為戶部郎中。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, Yong was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, Yong was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 張廷珪為黃門侍郎，而姜皎方幸，共援邕為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Zhang Tinggui served as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, and Jiang Jiao was then in favor; together they promoted Yong to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinggui served as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, and Jiang Jiao was then in favor; together they promoted Yong to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 姚崇疾邕險躁，左遷括州司馬，起為陳州刺史。

translations.literal: Yao Chong disliked Yong's rash and volatile character and transferred him to the post of Assistant Governor of Kuozhou; he was later recalled as Governor of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong disliked Yong's rash and volatile character and transferred him to Assistant Governor of Kuozhou; he was later recalled as Governor of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝封泰山還，邕見帝汴州，詔獻辭賦，帝悅。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from performing the feng and shan rites on Mount Tai, Yong met the emperor at Bianzhou; by edict he submitted a rhapsody, and the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from performing the feng and shan rites on Mount Tai, Yong met the emperor at Bianzhou, submitted a rhapsody by imperial command, and pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 然矜肆，自謂且宰相。

translations.literal: Yet he was arrogant and unrestrained, saying to himself that he would soon become chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was arrogant and unrestrained, telling himself that he would soon become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 邕素輕張說，與相惡。

translations.literal: Yong had long looked down on Zhang Yue, and the two detested each other.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had long looked down on Zhang Yue, and the two detested each other.

sentences.zh: 會仇人告邕贓貸枉法，下獄當死。

translations.literal: Then an enemy reported that Yong had taken bribes and perverted the law; he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Then an enemy reported that Yong had taken bribes and perverted the law; he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 許昌男子孔璋上書天子曰：

translations.literal: A man of Xuchang named Kong Zhang submitted a memorial to the Son of Heaven, saying:
translations.idiomatic: A man of Xuchang named Kong Zhang submitted a memorial to the Son of Heaven, saying:

sentences.zh: :明主舉能而捨過，取才而棄行，烈士抗節，勇者不避死，故晉用林父不以過，漢任陳平不以行，禽息隕身不祈生，北郭碎首不愛死。

translations.literal: A wise ruler promotes ability and overlooks faults, selects talent and sets aside conduct. A man of fierce integrity holds fast to principle; the brave do not shun death. Therefore Jin employed Xun Linfu despite his faults, and Han entrusted Chen Ping despite his conduct. Qin Xi gave up his life without praying to live; Bei Guo smashed his head without cherishing death.
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler promotes ability and overlooks faults, selects talent and sets aside personal conduct. A man of fierce integrity holds fast to principle; the brave do not shun death. Therefore Jin employed Xun Linfu despite his faults, and Han entrusted Chen Ping despite his character. Qin Xi gave up his life without praying to live; Bei Guo smashed his head without cherishing death.

sentences.zh: 向若林父誅，陳平死，百里不用，晏嬰見逐，是晉無赤狄之土，漢無天子之尊，秦不強，齊不霸矣。

translations.literal: If Linfu had been executed, Chen Ping had died, Baili Xi had not been employed, and Yan Ying had been driven away, then Jin would have had no lands of the Red Di, Han would have lacked the dignity of the Son of Heaven, Qin would not have grown strong, and Qi would not have become hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: If Linfu had been executed, Chen Ping had died, Baili Xi had not been employed, and Yan Ying had been driven away, then Jin would have had no lands of the Red Di, Han would have lacked the dignity of the Son of Heaven, Qin would not have grown strong, and Qi would not have become hegemon.

sentences.zh: 伏見陳州刺史邕，剛毅忠烈，難不苟免。

translations.literal: I humbly observe that Yong, Governor of Chenzhou, is resolute, loyal, and fierce, and would not seek to escape danger at the cost of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly observe that Yong, Governor of Chenzhou, is resolute, loyal, and fierce, and would not seek to escape danger at the cost of integrity.

sentences.zh: 往者折二張之角，挫韋氏之鋒，雖身受謫屈，而奸謀沮解，即邕有功于國。

translations.literal: In the past he broke the horns of the two Zhangs and blunted the edge of the Wei clan. Though he himself suffered demotion and humiliation, treacherous plots were thwarted and dissolved—this is Yong's service to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the past he broke the power of the two Zhangs and blunted the edge of the Wei clan. Though he himself suffered demotion and humiliation, treacherous plots were thwarted and dissolved—this is Yong's service to the state.

sentences.zh: 且邕所能者，拯孤恤窮，救乏賙急，家無私聚。

translations.literal: Moreover, what Yong is capable of is rescuing the orphaned and pitying the destitute, relieving want and aiding the urgent; his household keeps no private hoard.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what Yong excels at is rescuing the orphaned and pitying the destitute, relieving want and aiding the urgent; his household keeps no private hoard.

sentences.zh: 今聞坐贓下吏，死在旦夕。

translations.literal: Now I hear that for the charge of corruption he has been handed over to the officials, and death is imminent.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear that on a charge of corruption he has been handed over to the officials, and death is imminent.

sentences.zh: 臣聞生無益于國者，不若殺身以明賢。

translations.literal: I have heard that one who lives without benefit to the state is not as good as giving up his life to make clear the worth of a worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that one who lives without benefit to the state is not as good as giving up his life to make clear the worth of a worthy man.

sentences.zh: 臣願以六尺之軀膏鈇鉞，以代邕死。

translations.literal: I wish to offer my six-foot frame to the axe and halberd in place of Yong's death.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to offer my six-foot frame to the axe and halberd in place of Yong's death.

sentences.zh: 臣與邕生平不款曲，臣知有邕，邕不知有臣，臣不逮邕明矣。

translations.literal: Yong and I were never close in life; I know of Yong, but Yong does not know of me. That I do not measure up to Yong is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and I were never close in life; I know of Yong, but Yong does not know of me. That I do not measure up to Yong is clear.

sentences.zh: 夫知賢而舉，仁也；

translations.literal: To recognize worth and promote it is benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: To recognize worth and promote it is benevolence;

sentences.zh: 任人之患，義也。

translations.literal: to bear another's afflictions is righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: to bear another's afflictions is righteousness.

sentences.zh: 獲二善以死，臣又何求？

translations.literal: To obtain these two virtues and die—what more could your subject ask?
translations.idiomatic: To obtain these two virtues and die—what more could your subject ask?

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下寬邕之死，使率德改行。

translations.literal: I humbly ask Your Majesty to spare Yong from death and allow him to lead others in virtue and reform his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask Your Majesty to spare Yong from death and allow him to lead others in virtue and reform his conduct.

sentences.zh: 興林父、曲逆之功，臣得瞑目；

translations.literal: To revive the achievements of Linfu and the Marquis of Quyong—then your subject may close his eyes in peace;
translations.idiomatic: To revive the achievements of Linfu and the Marquis of Quyong—then your subject may close his eyes in peace;

sentences.zh: 附禽息、北郭之跡，大願畢矣。

translations.literal: to follow in the footsteps of Qin Xi and Bei Guo—then my great wish will be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: to follow in the footsteps of Qin Xi and Bei Guo—then my great wish will be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 若以陽和方始，重行大戮，則臣請伏劍，不敢煩有司，皇天后土，實聞臣言。

translations.literal: If, just as the warm spring is beginning, a great execution is carried out again, then your subject asks to submit to the sword and dares not trouble the officials. May Heaven and Earth hear my words.
translations.idiomatic: If, just as the warm spring is beginning, a great execution is carried out again, then your subject asks to submit to the sword and dares not trouble the officials. May Heaven and Earth hear my words.

sentences.zh: 昔吳、楚反，漢得劇孟則不憂，夫以一賢而敵七國之眾，伏惟敷含垢之道，棄瑕之義，遠思劇孟，近取於邕。

translations.literal: In the past, when Wu and Chu rebelled, Han had no worry once it obtained Jiemeng. With one worthy man to match the hosts of seven states, I humbly ask Your Majesty to spread the way of bearing disgrace and the principle of overlooking flaws—looking far to Jiemeng and taking Yong from nearer at hand.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when Wu and Chu rebelled, Han had no worry once it obtained Jiemeng. With one worthy man to match the hosts of seven states, I humbly ask Your Majesty to spread the way of bearing disgrace and the principle of overlooking flaws—looking far to Jiemeng and taking Yong from nearer at hand.

sentences.zh: 況告成岱宗，天地更新，赦而復論，人誰無罪，惟明主圖之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the announcement at Mount Tai is completed, heaven and earth are renewed—amnesty and reconsideration—who among men is without guilt? Only a wise ruler should ponder this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, now that the rites at Mount Tai are announced complete and heaven and earth are renewed, pardon and reconsideration are in order—who among men is without guilt? Only a wise ruler should weigh this.

sentences.zh: 臣聞士為知己者死，臣不為死者所知，而甘之死者，非特惜邕賢，亦以成陛下矜能之慈。

translations.literal: I have heard that a gentleman dies for one who knows him. Your subject is unknown to the one who dies, yet willingly dies—not only cherishing Yong's worth, but also to fulfill Your Majesty's compassionate regard for ability.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a gentleman dies for one who knows him. Your subject is unknown to the man for whom he dies, yet he willingly dies—not only out of regard for Yong's talent, but also to complete Your Majesty's merciful esteem for ability.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，邕得減死，貶遵化尉，流璋嶺南。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Yong's death sentence was commuted; he was demoted to Warden of Zunhua, and Zhang was exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Yong's death sentence was reduced; he was demoted to warden of Zunhua, and Zhang was exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 邕妻溫，復為邕請戍邊自贖，曰：

translations.literal: Yong's wife Wen again pleaded for Yong to redeem himself by frontier guard duty, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yong's wife, the Wen clan, again petitioned that Yong might redeem himself by serving on the frontier, saying:

sentences.zh: :邕少習文章，疾惡如仇，不容於眾，邪佞切齒，諸儒側目。

translations.literal: Yong from youth studied literature, hated evil as if it were a personal enemy, could not be tolerated by the multitude; the wicked gnashed their teeth, the scholars glared sidelong.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yong trained in letters and hated wickedness as he would a personal foe; the crowd could not tolerate him, the sycophantic gnashed their teeth, and the literati glared at him sidelong.

sentences.zh: 頻謫遠郡，削跡朝端，不啻十載。

translations.literal: Repeatedly demoted to distant commanderies, erased from the court, no less than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly demoted to distant prefectures and vanished from the capital for no less than ten years.

sentences.zh: 歲時歎戀，聞者傷懷。

translations.literal: Each year sighing with longing—those who heard were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he sighed with longing, and those who heard it were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 屬國家有事泰山，法駕旋路，邕獻牛酒，例蒙恩私。

translations.literal: When the state had business at Mount Tai, as the imperial carriage returned on its route, Yong presented oxen and wine and by custom received private favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the state undertook the rites at Mount Tai and the imperial carriage returned by its route, Yong presented oxen and wine and, by precedent, received a private grant of favor.

sentences.zh: 妾聞正人用則佞人憂，邕之禍端，故自此始。

translations.literal: Your handmaid heard that when upright men are employed, sycophants fret—the beginning of Yong's disaster therefore started here.
translations.idiomatic: Your handmaid has heard that when upright men are put to use, flatterers grow anxious; the root of Yong's calamity began here.

sentences.zh: 且邕比任外官，卒無一毀，天意暫顧，罪過旋生。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Yong's recent tenure as outer official, in the end there was not one reproach—heaven's favor briefly looked upon him, and guilt immediately arose.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in Yong's recent service as an outer official, in the end there was not a single charge against him; heaven briefly favored him, and guilt sprang up at once.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：「士無賢不肖，入朝見疾。」

translations.literal: A proverb says: "Whether a gentleman is worthy or unworthy, once he enters court he meets with hatred.
translations.idiomatic: A proverb says, "Whether a gentleman is worthy or base, once he enters court he meets with hatred.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下明察。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty discern clearly.
translations.idiomatic: I ask only that Your Majesty see clearly.

sentences.zh: 邕初蒙訊責，便繫牢戶，水不入口者逾五日，氣息奄奄，惟吏是聽。

translations.literal: When Yong first faced interrogation and blame, he was immediately shackled in a prison cell; for more than five days he did not take water, his breath faint and feeble, at the mercy of the clerks alone.
