translations.idiomatic: When Yong first faced interrogation, he was at once bound in a prison cell; for more than five days he took no water, his breath grew faint, and he had only the clerks to obey.

sentences.zh: 事生吏口，迫邕手書。

translations.literal: The affair arose from the clerks' mouths; they forced Yong to write with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: The case sprang from the clerks' mouths, and they compelled Yong to write it out in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 貸人蠶種，以為枉法；

translations.literal: Lending someone silkworm seed was taken as perverting the law;
translations.idiomatic: Lending someone silkworm seed was treated as bending the law;

sentences.zh: 市羅貢奉，指為奸贓。

translations.literal: Buying silk for tribute was pointed to as corrupt bribery.
translations.idiomatic: buying silk for tribute was called corrupt bribery.

sentences.zh: 于時匭使朝堂，守捉嚴固，號天訴地，誰肯為聞？

translations.literal: At that time casket-messengers were at court, guards strict and firm—he cried to heaven and appealed to earth; who would speak for him?
translations.idiomatic: At that time the casket-messengers were at court and the guards were strict; he cried to heaven and appealed to earth, yet who would report it for him?

sentences.zh: 泣血去國，投身荒裔，永無還期。

translations.literal: Weeping blood he left the state, cast himself into the wild borderlands, never to have a date of return.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping blood, he left the realm, cast himself into the wild borderlands, and would never again have a day of return.

sentences.zh: 妾願使邕得充一卒，效力王事，膏塗朔邊，骨糞沙壤，成邕夙心。

translations.literal: Your handmaid wishes that Yong may serve as a single soldier, exerting strength for the king's affairs, smearing his flesh on the northern frontier, his bones fertilizing sandy soil, fulfilling Yong's long-held wish.
translations.idiomatic: Your handmaid asks that Yong be allowed to serve as a common soldier, to give his strength to the king's service, to smear his flesh on the northern marches and let his bones manure the sandy soil, fulfilling Yong's lifelong wish.

sentences.zh: 表入不省。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no response.

sentences.zh: 邕後從中人楊思勖討嶺南賊有功，徙澧州司馬。

translations.literal: Later Yong followed the inner eunuch Yang Sixu in punishing the bandits of Lingnan and had merit; he was transferred to Administrator of Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yong followed the palace eunuch Yang Sixu in campaigning against the Lingnan rebels and won merit; he was transferred to administrator of Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年，起為括州刺史，喜興利除害。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, he was recalled to be Prefect of Kuozhou, delighting in promoting benefit and removing harm.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan he was recalled as prefect of Kuozhou, where he delighted in promoting what benefited the people and removing what harmed them.

sentences.zh: 復坐誣枉，且得罪，天子識其名，詔勿劾。

translations.literal: Again he sat under false accusation and was about to be punished; the Son of Heaven recognized his name and ordered that he not be impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Again he was charged on false grounds and was about to be punished, but the Son of Heaven knew his name and ordered that he not be impeached.

sentences.zh: 後歷淄、滑二州刺史，上計京師。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Prefect of Zi and Hua, and presented his accounts in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in succession as prefect of Zi and Hua and came to the capital to present his annual accounts.

sentences.zh: 始，邕蚤有名，重義愛士，久斥外，不與士大夫接。

translations.literal: At first, Yong had early achieved fame, valued righteousness and loved scholars; long expelled outside, he did not associate with court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: From the first Yong had won fame early, prized righteousness, and loved men of talent; long banished outside, he had no contact with court scholars.

sentences.zh: 既入朝，人間傳其眉目瑰異，至阡陌聚觀，後生望風內謁，門巷填隘。

translations.literal: Once he entered court, the world spread word that his features were wondrous and strange; even along the lanes crowds gathered to watch; younger men, catching wind of him, came to call within; lanes and alleys were jammed full.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered court, word spread that his face was striking and strange; crowds gathered even along the lanes to watch, young men came in throngs at the mere rumor of him, and streets and alleys were packed tight.

sentences.zh: 中人臨問，索所為文章，且進上。

translations.literal: Eunuchs came to inquire, seeking his writings and requesting them to be presented upward.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs came to question him, demanded his writings, and had them presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 以讒媢不得留，出為汲郡、北海太守。

translations.literal: Because of slander and jealousy he could not remain, and went out as Administrator of Jijun and Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Because of slander and envy he could not remain at court and was sent out as administrator of Jijun and then Beihai.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，左驍衛兵曹參軍柳勣有罪下獄，邕嘗遺勣馬，故吉溫使引邕嘗以休咎相語，陰賂遺。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, Left Brave Cavalry Guard army officer Liu Li had a crime and was imprisoned; Yong had once given Ji a horse, so Ji Wen caused Yong to be implicated for having spoken with him about fortune and misfortune, with secret bribery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao period, Liu Li, army officer of the Left Brave Cavalry Guard, was imprisoned for a crime; Yong had once given Li a horse, so Ji Wen had Li implicate Yong for having privately discussed omens and fortunes and for secret bribes.

sentences.zh: 宰相李林甫素忌邕，因傅以罪。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Linfu had long resented Yong, and accordingly piled on charges.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor Li Linfu had long resented Yong and accordingly heaped charges upon him.

sentences.zh: 詔刑部員外郎祁順之、監察御史羅希奭就郡杖殺之，時年七十。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ministry of Punishments Vice Director Qi Shunzhi and Supervising Censor Luo Xi'a to go to his commandery and beat him to death with the staff; he was then seventy years old.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Qi Shunzhi, vice director of the Ministry of Punishments, and the supervising censor Luo Xi'a to go to his prefecture and beat him to death with the staff; he was then seventy.

sentences.zh: 代宗時，贈秘書監。

translations.literal: In the Daizong period, he was posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daizong reign he was posthumously made director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 邕之文，於碑頌是所長，人奉金帛請其文，前後所受鉅萬計。

translations.literal: Yong's writing—in stele inscriptions and eulogies was his strength; people presented gold and silk to request his compositions; before and after, what he received amounted to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In stele inscriptions and eulogies Yong's writing was strongest; people offered gold and silk to commission his texts, and over time what he received ran to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 邕雖詘不進，而文名天下，時稱李北海。

translations.literal: Though Yong was demoted and not advanced, his literary name filled the realm; of the time he was called Li of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yong was demoted and did not advance in office, his literary fame filled the realm, and men of the time called him Li of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 盧藏用嘗謂：「邕如干將、莫邪，難與爭鋒，但虞傷缺耳。」

translations.literal: Lu Zangyong once said: "Yong is like Ganjiang and Moye—hard to compete with in edge; only fear a chip in the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zangyong once said, "Yong is like Ganjiang and Moye: hard to rival in sharpness, but one fears a nick in the blade.

sentences.zh: 後卒如言。

translations.literal: Later he died exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died exactly as Zangyong had said.

sentences.zh: 杜甫知邕負謗死，作《八哀詩》，讀者傷之。

translations.literal: Du Fu, knowing Yong died bearing calumny, composed "The Eight Laments"; readers were grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fu, knowing that Yong had died under false charges, wrote the "Eight Laments," and readers were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 邕資豪放，不能治細行，所在賄謝，畋遊自肆，終以敗云。

translations.literal: Yong by nature was bold and unrestrained, could not govern small conduct; wherever he was, bribes and gifts, hunting and roaming at will—ultimately he failed thus.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Yong was bold and unrestrained and could not keep to small proprieties; wherever he served he accepted gifts, hunted, and roamed at will, and in the end he was ruined for it.

sentences.zh: 呂向呂向，字子回，亡其世貫，或曰涇州人。

translations.literal: Lu Xiang. Lu Xiang, courtesy name Zihui, lost knowledge of his lineage; some say he was a man of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiang—Lu Xiang, courtesy name Zihui, had lost track of his lineage; some say he was from Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少孤，托外祖母隱陸渾山。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he relied on his maternal grandmother and lived hidden on Mount Luhun.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised by his maternal grandmother and lived in seclusion on Mount Luhun.

sentences.zh: 工草隸，能一筆環寫百字，若縈發然，世號「連錦書」。

translations.literal: Skilled in draft and clerical script, able to write a hundred characters in one continuous ring as if coiled hair; the age called it "Linked Brocade Script."
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in draft and clerical script and could write a hundred characters in one unbroken ring, as if coiling hair; his age called it "linked brocade script."

sentences.zh: 強志於學，每賣藥，即市閱書，遂通古今。

translations.literal: Strong of will in study; whenever he sold medicine, he at once went to the marketplace to read books, and thus mastered past and present.
translations.idiomatic: He was fiercely intent on learning; whenever he sold medicine he would at once go to the market to read books, and so came to know past and present.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元十年，召入翰林，兼集賢院校理，侍太子及諸王為文章。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan of Xuanzong, summoned into the Hanlin Academy, concurrently collator at the Academy of Assembled Worthies, attending the Crown Prince and various princes in composition.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan, Xuanzong summoned him into the Hanlin Academy and made him concurrently a collator at the Academy of Assembled Worthies, where he composed for the crown prince and the princes.

sentences.zh: 時帝歲遣使采擇天下姝好，內之後宮，號「花鳥使」；

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor each year sent envoys to select the finest beauties of the realm for the inner palace, titled "Flower-and-Bird Envoy";
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor each year sent envoys to gather the finest beauties in the land for the inner palace, called the "flower-and-bird envoys";

sentences.zh: 向因奏《美人賦》以諷，帝善之，擢左拾遺。

translations.literal: Xiang therefore submitted "Rhapsody on the Beauty" as remonstrance; the Emperor was pleased with it and promoted him to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang therefore submitted the "Rhapsody on the Beauty" as indirect remonstrance; the emperor approved it and promoted him to left reminder.

sentences.zh: 天子數校獵渭川，向又獻詩規諷，進左補闕。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven repeatedly held hunts on the Wei River; Xiang again presented verse admonishing, and was advanced to Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven repeatedly hunted on the Wei River; Xiang again submitted verse of admonition and was advanced to left supplementation censor.

sentences.zh: 帝自為文，勒石西嶽，詔向為鐫勒使。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself composed a text and had it carved on stone at West Peak; he ordered Xiang to be stone-engraving commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself wrote a text and had it carved in stone on the western sacred peak; he appointed Xiang commissioner for the engraving.

sentences.zh: 以起居舍人從帝東巡，帝引頡利發及蕃夷酋長入仗內，賜弓矢射禽。

translations.literal: As Attendant on the Imperial Diary he followed the Emperor on the eastern tour; the Emperor led Ashina Fa and chieftains of various barbarians into the bodyguard, bestowing bows and arrows to shoot game.
translations.idiomatic: As attendant on the imperial diary he followed the emperor on the eastern tour; the emperor brought Ashina Fa and chieftains of various foreign peoples into the guard formation and gave them bows and arrows to shoot game.

sentences.zh: 向上言：「鴟梟不鳴，未為瑞鳥；

translations.literal: Xiang spoke upward: "The owl does not cry—yet it is not called an auspicious bird;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang submitted: "The owl does not cry, yet it is not called an auspicious bird;

sentences.zh: 豺虎雖伏，弗曰仁獸。

translations.literal: The wolf and tiger though crouching—one does not call them benevolent beasts.
translations.idiomatic: the wolf and tiger may crouch low, yet one does not call them benevolent beasts.

sentences.zh: 況突厥安忍殘賊，莫顧君父，陛下震以武義，來以文德，勢不得不廷，故稽顙稱臣，奔命遣使。

translations.literal: Moreover the Turks are cruel and patient in injury, heedless of lord and father; Your Majesty with martial righteousness awes them and with civil virtue draws them—so their power cannot but attend court; therefore they bow forehead and declare themselves subjects, rushing orders and dispatching envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Turks are cruel and endure injury without regard for lord or father; Your Majesty awes them with martial righteousness and draws them with civil virtue, so that they cannot but come to court; therefore they bow their foreheads, declare themselves subjects, and rush to send envoys.

sentences.zh: 陛下引內從官，陪封禪盛禮，使飛矢於前，同獲獸之樂，是狎昵太過。

translations.literal: Your Majesty draws them within to follow officials, joining in the grand rites of the Feng and Shan—letting flying arrows before them, sharing the joy of taking game together—this is excessive intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty brings them inside to attend your officials and share in the grand rites of the Feng and Shan, letting arrows fly before them and sharing the joy of the hunt—this is intimacy carried too far.

sentences.zh: 或荊卿詭動，何羅竊發，逼嚴蹕，冒清塵，縱醢單于，汙穹廬，何以塞責？」

translations.literal: Or like Jing Ke's crafty stir, or He Luo's stealthy outbreak—pressing close upon the imperial guard, defiling the clear dust—letting them mince the Chanyu, befoul the royal tent—how would one answer for it?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose Jing Ke's cunning stir or He Luo's stealthy strike should come—pressing upon the imperial guard, befouling the clear road—allowing them to hack apart the Chanyu and stain the royal tent: how would Your Majesty answer for it?

sentences.zh: 帝順納，詔蕃夷出仗。

translations.literal: The Emperor yielded and accepted; ordered the barbarians out of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented and ordered the foreign chieftains removed from the guard formation.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷主客郎中，專侍皇太子，眷賚良異。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was transferred to Director of the Office of the Chief Guest, exclusively attending the Crown Prince; favors and gifts were exceptionally fine.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was transferred to director of the Office of the Chief Guest, where he attended exclusively on the crown prince and received unusually rich favors and gifts.

sentences.zh: 始，向之生，父岌客遠方不還。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Xiang was born, his father Ji was a guest in distant places and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, when Xiang was born, his father Ji was traveling in distant places and did not return.

sentences.zh: 少喪母，失墓所在，將葬，巫者求得之。

translations.literal: He lost his mother young; the grave's location was unknown; when about to bury, the shaman found it.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother young and did not know where her grave lay; when he was about to bury her, a shaman located it.

sentences.zh: 不知父在亡，招魂合諸墓。

translations.literal: Not knowing whether his father was alive or dead, he summoned the soul and combined it with the graves.
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing whether his father was alive or dead, he performed a soul-summoning rite and joined it to the graves.

sentences.zh: 後有傳父猶在者，訪索累年不獲。

translations.literal: Later there was word that his father was still alive; he searched for many years without finding him.
translations.idiomatic: Later word came that his father was still alive, and he searched for many years without finding him.

sentences.zh: 它日自朝還，道見一老人，物色問之，果父也。

translations.literal: One day returning from court on the road, he saw an old man, scrutinized and questioned him—it was indeed his father.
translations.idiomatic: One day, returning from court on the road, he saw an old man, scrutinized him, and questioned him—it was indeed his father.

sentences.zh: 下馬抱父足號慟，行人為流涕。

translations.literal: He dismounted and embraced his father's feet, wailing bitterly; passersby shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted, clasped his father's feet, and wailed bitterly; passersby wept.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，咨歎，官岌朝散大夫，賜錦彩，給內教坊樂工，娛懌其心。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he sighed in sympathy, appointed Ji Court Gentleman for Scattered Service, bestowed brocade and silk, and gave musicians of the inner Music Office to delight his heart.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he sighed in admiration, appointed Ji court gentleman for scattered service, bestowed brocade and silk, and gave him musicians from the inner music office to delight his heart.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈東平太守。

translations.literal: At death, he was posthumously granted Administrator of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made administrator of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 向終喪，再遷中書舍人，改工部侍郎。

translations.literal: After Xiang's mourning period ended, he was again promoted to Palace Secretariat Drafting Official, changed to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang's mourning ended, he was again promoted to drafting official of the Palace Secretariat and then transferred to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈華陰太守。

translations.literal: At death, posthumously granted Administrator of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made administrator of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 嘗以李善釋《文選》為繁釀，與呂延濟、劉良、張銑、李周翰等更為詁解，時號《五臣注》。

translations.literal: He once regarded Li Shan's commentary on the "Wen Xuan" as overly elaborate, and with Lü Yanji, Liu Liang, Zhang Xian, Li Zhouhan and others made a new gloss—of the time called the "Five Ministers' Commentary."
translations.idiomatic: He once found Li Shan's commentary on the Wen Xuan too elaborate and, with Lü Yanji, Liu Liang, Zhang Xian, Li Zhouhan, and others, produced a new gloss that men of the time called the Five Ministers' Commentary.

sentences.zh: 王翰王翰，字子羽，并州晉陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Han. Wang Han, courtesy name Ziyu, a native of Jinyang in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han—Wang Han, courtesy name Ziyu, was a native of Jinyang in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少豪健恃才，及進士第，然喜蒱酒。

translations.literal: In youth bold and hardy, relying on talent; after obtaining the jinshi degree, yet he loved dice and wine.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was bold and relied on his talent; after passing the jinshi examination he still loved gambling and wine.

sentences.zh: 張嘉貞為本州長史，偉其人，厚遇之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiaying was Chief Administrator of this circuit, admired the man, and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiaying was chief administrator of the circuit; he admired Han and treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 翰自歌以舞屬嘉貞，神氣軒舉自如。

translations.literal: Han himself sang and danced for Jiaying, his spirit lofty and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Han himself sang and danced for Jiaying, his bearing lofty and utterly at ease.

sentences.zh: 張說至，禮益加。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yue arrived, courtesy was even more increased.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue arrived, the courtesy shown him grew even greater.

sentences.zh: 復舉直言極諫，調昌樂尉，又舉超拔君類。

translations.literal: Again nominated for "Straightforward and Remonstrating to the Utmost," transferred to Warden of Changle; again nominated for "Outstanding and Advancing Junzi Categories."
translations.idiomatic: He was again nominated for the "straightforward and remonstrating to the utmost" examination and appointed warden of Changle; he was again nominated for "outstanding and advancing worthy categories."

sentences.zh: 方說輔政，故召為秘書正字，擢通事舍人、駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: As Yue was then assisting in government, he was therefore summoned as Proofreader of the Secretariat, promoted to Palace Gate Messenger and Deputy Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yue was then assisting in government, Han was summoned as proofreader of the Secretariat and promoted to palace gate messenger and deputy director of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 家畜聲伎，目使頤令，自視王侯，人莫不惡之。

translations.literal: His household kept singing girls; he ordered them about at will, viewing himself as equal to kings and marquises—people all hated him.
translations.idiomatic: His household kept singing girls whom he ordered about at will; he regarded himself as the equal of kings and marquises, and everyone detested him.

sentences.zh: 說罷宰相，翰出為汝州長史，徙仙州別駕。

translations.literal: When Yue left the chancellorship, Han went out as Administrator of Ruzhou, transferred to Vice Prefect of Xianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue left the chancellorship, Han was sent out as administrator of Ruzhou and later transferred to vice prefect of Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 日與才士豪俠飲樂游畋，伐鼓窮歡，坐貶道州司馬，卒。

translations.literal: Daily with talented gentlemen, bold heroes, drinking, music, touring and hunting—beating drums to exhaust joy—he sat and was demoted to Libo's Administrator, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he drank, made music, toured, and hunted with talented gentlemen and bold heroes, beating drums until joy was spent; for this he was demoted to administrator of Daozhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 孫逖孫逖，博州武水人。

translations.literal: Sun Ti. Sun Ti, a man of Wushui in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ti—Sun Ti was a man of Wushui in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 後魏光祿大夫惠蔚，其先也。

translations.literal: Huiwei, Director of Imperial Brightness of Later Wei, was his ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor was Huiwei, director of imperial brightness under Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖希壯，為韓王府典簽，四世傳一子，故無近屬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xizhuang was secretary of the Prince of Han's household; for four generations one son was passed down, hence no near kin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xizhuang had been secretary of the Prince of Han's household; for four generations only one son was born in each, so the family had no close relatives.

sentences.zh: 父嘉之，少孤，依外家，客涉、鞏間。

translations.literal: His father Jianzhi, orphaned young, relied on his maternal family, guesting between She and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jianzhi was orphaned young, relied on his mother's family, and lived as a guest between She and Gong.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，詣洛陽獻書，不報。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chuigong, he went to Luoyang to present a book; no reply.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chuigong era he went to Luoyang to present a book and received no answer.

sentences.zh: 第進士，終襄邑令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and ended as Magistrate of Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and ended his career as magistrate of Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 逖幼有文，屬思警敏。

translations.literal: Ti in youth had literary gift; his marshaling of thought was sharp and nimble.
translations.idiomatic: Ti showed literary talent in youth and marshaled his thoughts with quick, keen wit.

sentences.zh: 年十五，見雍州長史崔日用，令賦土火爐，援筆成篇，理趣不凡，日用駭歎，遂與定交。

translations.literal: At fifteen he saw Chief Administrator Cui Riyong of Yongzhou, who ordered him to compose on the "Earth-Fire Stove"; he took brush and finished the piece; reasoning and interest were uncommon; Riyong was startled and admired, and thereupon formed a bond.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he met Cui Riyong, chief administrator of Yong Prefecture, who ordered him to compose on the "earth-fire stove"; he took up the brush and finished the piece at once, with reasoning and tone far above the ordinary; Riyong was astonished and admired him, and they became close friends.

sentences.zh: 舉手筆俊拔、哲人奇士、隱淪屠釣及文藻宏麗等科。

translations.literal: He was nominated for the examinations Handwriting Outstandingly Promoted, Sage-like Men and Extraordinary Scholars, Recluses Butchers Anglers, and Literary Splendor Magnificent and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was nominated for the examinations for outstanding brushwork, sage-like and extraordinary scholars, recluses, butchers, and anglers, and for literary splendor, among others.

sentences.zh: 開元十年，又舉賢良方正。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan, again nominated for Worthy and Able Upright.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan he was again nominated for worthy and upright.

sentences.zh: 玄宗禦洛城門引見，命戶部郎中蘇晉等第其文異等，擢左拾遺。

translations.literal: Xuanzong received audience at Luocheng Gate; he ordered Household Department Director Su Jin and others to rank his writing highest grade; he was promoted to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong received him in audience at Luocheng Gate, ordered Su Jin of the household department and others to rank his writing in the highest class, and promoted him to left reminder.

sentences.zh: 張說命子均、垍往拜之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue ordered his sons Jun and Kai to go pay court to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue ordered his sons Jun and Kai to call on him.

sentences.zh: 李邕負才，自陳州入計，裒其文示逖。

translations.literal: Li Yong, carrying talent, came from Chenzhou to present accounts, gathered his writings and showed them to Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong, confident in his talent, came from Chen Prefecture to present his accounts, gathered his writings, and showed them to Ti.

sentences.zh: 李暠鎮太原，表置幕府。

translations.literal: When Li Gao was stationed at Taiyuan, he submitted a memorial to place Ti in his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gao was stationed at Taiyuan, he memorialized to place Ti on his staff.

sentences.zh: 以起居舍人入為集賢院脩撰。

translations.literal: As Attendant on the Imperial Diary he entered to serve as compiler and editor at the Academy of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: As attendant on the imperial diary he entered court to serve as compiler and editor at the Academy of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 時海內少事，帝賜群臣十日一燕，宰相蕭嵩會百官賦《天成》、《玄澤》、《維南有山》、《楊之華》、《三月》、《英英有蘭》、《和風》、《嘉木》等詩八篇，繼《雅》、《頌》體，使逖序所以然。

translations.literal: At that time within the seas affairs were few; the Emperor granted ministers a feast every ten days; Chancellor Xiao Song and all officials composed eight poems including "Heaven Complete," "Mysterious Grace," "South the Mountain," "Yang's Splendor," "Third Month," "Orchid Abundant," "Harmonious Wind," and "Fine Trees"—following the style of Ya and Song; he had Ti preface their rationale.
translations.idiomatic: At that time affairs within the realm were few; the emperor granted the ministers a feast every ten days; the chancellor Xiao Song and all the officials composed eight poems—including "Heaven Complete," "Mysterious Grace," "South the Mountain," "Yang's Splendor," "Third Month," "Orchid Abundant," "Harmonious Wind," and "Fine Trees"—in the manner of the Ya and Song sections, and had Ti write prefaces explaining their intent.

sentences.zh: 改考功員外郎，取顏真卿、李華、蕭穎士、趙驊等，皆海內有名士。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel; he selected Yan Zhenqing, Li Hua, Xiao Yingshi, Zhao Hua and others—all were famous gentlemen within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, where he selected Yan Zhenqing, Li Hua, Xiao Yingshi, Zhao Hua, and others—all renowned men within the realm.

sentences.zh: 俄遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Palace Secretariat Drafting Official.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made drafting official of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是時，嘉之且八十，猶為令，逖求降外官，增父秩。

translations.literal: At this time Jianzhi was nearly eighty, still serving as magistrate; Ti requested demotion to an outer post to increase his father's rank.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Jianzhi was nearly eighty and still serving as a magistrate; Ti asked to take a lower outer post so that his father's rank might be raised.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納，拜嘉之宋州司馬，聽致仕。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended and accepted; appointed Jianzhi Military Aide of Song Prefecture, permitting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and commended him, appointed Jianzhi military aide of Song Prefecture, and allowed him to retire.

sentences.zh: 父喪闋，復拜舍人。

translations.literal: After the mourning period for his father ended, he was again appointed Drafting Official.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning for his father was finished, he was again appointed drafting official.

sentences.zh: 開元間，蘇頲、齊浣、蘇晉、賈曾、韓休、許景先及逖典詔誥，為代言最，而逖尤精密，張九齡視其草，欲易一字，卒不能也。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan, Su Ting, Qi Huan, Su Jin, Jia Ceng, Han Xiu, Xu Jingxian and Ti together drafted edicts—they were the foremost in ghostwriting, but Ti was especially precise; Zhang Jiuling looked at his draft and wished to change a single character, but in the end could not.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, Su Ting, Qi Huan, Su Jin, Jia Ceng, Han Xiu, Xu Jingxian, and Ti together drafted imperial edicts; they were foremost among the drafters, but Ti was especially exact—Zhang Jiuling looked at his draft and wished to change a single character, yet in the end could not.

sentences.zh: 居職八年，判刑部侍郎，以病風乞解，徙太子左庶子，遂綿廢累年，徙少詹事。

translations.literal: Eight years in office, sentenced as Vice Minister of Punishments; because of wind illness he begged to be relieved, transferred to Left Tutor of the Crown Prince; then languished in dismissal for many years, transferred to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years in office he was appointed vice minister of punishments; because of wind illness he asked to be relieved, was transferred to left tutor of the crown prince, then languished in enforced idleness for many years before being made junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 上元中卒，贈尚書右僕射，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He died in the Shangyuan period, posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Shangyuan period and was posthumously made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 諸子成最知名。

translations.literal: Among the sons, Cheng was most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Among Sun Ti's sons, Cheng was the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 子 成成，字思退，推廕仕累洛陽、長安令。

translations.literal: His son Cheng—Cheng's name was Cheng, courtesy name Sirui—entered office through yin privilege and successively served as magistrate of Luoyang and Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cheng, courtesy name Sirui, entered office through yin privilege and served in succession as magistrate of Luoyang and Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 兄宿為華州刺史，因悸病喑，成請告往視，不待報輒行，代宗嘉其悌，不責也。

translations.literal: His older brother Su was governor of Hua Prefecture; because of palpitations he had lost his voice; Cheng requested leave to go visit him, and without waiting for a reply set out; Daizong praised his filial devotion and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Su was governor of Hua Prefecture; stricken with palpitations, he had lost his voice. Cheng asked for leave to visit him and set out without waiting for approval. Daizong commended his filial devotion and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 稍遷倉部郎中、京兆少尹。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Director of the Warehouses Department and Junior Assistant of the Capital Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to director of the Warehouses Department and junior assistant of the capital metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為信州刺史，歲大旱，發倉以賤直售民，故饑而不亡。

translations.literal: As governor of Xin Prefecture, in a year of great drought he opened the granaries and sold grain to the people at low prices, so though there was famine the people did not perish.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Xin Prefecture, in a year of severe drought he opened the granaries and sold grain to the people at reduced prices, so that although famine struck, the people did not perish.

sentences.zh: 再期增戶五千，詔書褒美。

translations.literal: At the end of a second term of office the population increased by five thousand households; an imperial edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of a second term the registered population had increased by five thousand households, and an imperial edict commended him.

sentences.zh: 徙蘇州，改桂管觀察使，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Suzhou, then changed to military governor of Gui Pass, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Suzhou, then reassigned as military governor of Gui Pass, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 成通經術，奏議據正。

translations.literal: Cheng was versed in the classics, and his memorials and proposals were anchored in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was versed in the classics, and his memorials and proposals were firmly grounded in principle.

sentences.zh: 嘗有期喪，吊者至，成不易縗而見。

translations.literal: Once when he was in the intermediate mourning period, when mourners arrived Cheng did not change out of his hemp mourning garments to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while he was in the intermediate mourning period, when mourners arrived Cheng did not change out of his hemp mourning garments to receive them.

sentences.zh: 客疑之，請故，答曰：「縗者，古居喪常服，去之則廢喪也。

translations.literal: A guest was puzzled and asked the reason; he replied: "The hemp garment is the customary dress of ancient mourning; to remove it is to abandon mourning.
translations.idiomatic: A guest was puzzled and asked why; he replied, "The hemp garment is the customary dress of mourning in antiquity; to remove it is to abandon mourning.

sentences.zh: 今而巾襆，失矣。」

translations.literal: Now if one wears a headcloth and kerchief, that is a lapse."
translations.idiomatic: To wear a headcloth and kerchief instead is a lapse."

sentences.zh: 子公器，亦至邕管經略使。

translations.literal: His son was Gongqi, who also rose to military commissioner of Yong and Gui passes.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongqi also rose to military commissioner of Yong and Gui passes.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 簡公器子簡，字樞中。

translations.literal: A great-grandson was Jian—Gongqi's son Jian, courtesy name Shuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: A great-grandson was Jian—Gongqi's son Jian, courtesy name Shuzhong.

sentences.zh: 元和初，登進士第，辟鎮國、荊南幕府。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanhe period he passed the jinshi examination and was summoned to the staffs of Zhenguo and Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuanhe period he passed the jinshi examination and entered the staffs of Zhenguo and Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 累遷左司、吏部二郎中，繇諫議大夫知制誥，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Left Director and the two Directors of the Ministry of Personnel, from Remonstrance Grand Counselor with charge of drafting edicts to Drafting Official of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to left director and the two directors of the Ministry of Personnel, from remonstrance grand counselor with charge of drafting edicts to drafting official of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，逖掌誥，至代宗時，宿又居職，逮簡凡三世。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ti had handled edicts; by Daizong's time Su again held the post—counting Jian, three generations in all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ti had handled edicts; by Daizong's time Su again held the post—counting Jian, the family held it for three generations.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，遷尚書左丞，建言：

translations.literal: In the early Huichang period he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and submitted a proposal:
translations.idiomatic: In the early Huichang period he was promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and submitted a proposal:

sentences.zh: 班位以品秩為等差，今官兼台省，位置遷誤，不可為法。

translations.literal: Court precedence should be graded by rank; now when one officeholder concurrently holds a Chancellery or Secretariat post, seating is transposed in error and cannot serve as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Court precedence should be graded by rank and title; yet when an official concurrently holds a Chancellery or Secretariat post, seating is assigned in error and cannot serve as precedent.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，御史台白奏，常參官兼大夫、中丞者，視檢校官，居本品同類官上。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe the Censorate reported that regular attendees who concurrently held grand counselor or vice censor-in-chief posts were treated as acting officials and seated above others of the same substantive rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe the Censorate reported that regular attendees who concurrently held grand counselor or vice censor-in-chief posts were treated as acting officials and seated above others of the same substantive rank.

sentences.zh: 其後侍郎兼大夫者，皆在左、右丞上。

translations.literal: Afterward, vice ministers who concurrently held grand counselor posts all sat above the left and right vice directors.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, vice ministers who concurrently held grand counselor posts all sat above the left and right vice directors.

sentences.zh: 當時侍郎兼大夫少，唯京兆尹兼之。

translations.literal: At that time few vice ministers concurrently held grand counselor posts; only the capital metropolitan prefect did so.
translations.idiomatic: At that time few vice ministers concurrently held grand counselor posts; only the capital metropolitan prefect did so.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹從三品，今位乃在本品同類官從三品卿、監上，太常、宗正卿正三品下。

translations.literal: The capital metropolitan prefect was third rank, lower grade; now his seat was above others of the same substantive third rank, lower grade—the directors of the directorates and the supervisors—and below the directors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Court of the Imperial Clan, third rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: The capital metropolitan prefect was third rank, lower grade; yet his seat was now above others of the same substantive third rank, lower grade—the directors of the directorates and the supervisors—and below the directors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Court of the Imperial Clan, third rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 左丞乃正四品上，戶部侍郎正四品下，今戶部侍郎兼大夫當在本品同類正四品下，諸曹侍郎上，不宜居正四品丞、郎上。

translations.literal: The left vice director was fourth rank, upper grade; the vice minister of the Household Department was fourth rank, lower grade; now the vice minister of the Household Department who concurrently held grand counselor should have been among those of the same substantive fourth rank, lower grade, above the various vice ministers, and should not have sat above the fourth-rank vice directors and directors.
translations.idiomatic: The left vice director was fourth rank, upper grade; the vice minister of the Household Department was fourth rank, lower grade; yet the vice minister of the Household Department who concurrently held grand counselor now sat above the fourth-rank vice directors and directors, when he should have ranked among those of the same substantive fourth rank, lower grade, above the various vice ministers but below the vice directors.

sentences.zh: 又右丞正四品下，吏部侍郎正四品上，今吏部侍郎位右丞之下。

translations.literal: Moreover the right vice director was fourth rank, lower grade; the vice minister of the Personnel Department was fourth rank, upper grade; now the vice minister of the Personnel Department sat below the right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the right vice director was fourth rank, lower grade, while the vice minister of the Personnel Department was fourth rank, upper grade; yet the vice minister of the Personnel Department now sat below the right vice director.

sentences.zh: 蓋以丞有繩轄之重，雖吏部品高，猶居其下，然則戶部侍郎雖兼大夫，安得居其上哉？

translations.literal: This was because the vice director had the weight of restraint and oversight; even though the Personnel vice minister's rank was higher, he still sat below—then how could the Household vice minister, though concurrently grand counselor, sit above him?
translations.idiomatic: This was because the vice director bore the weight of restraint and oversight; even though the Personnel vice minister outranked him, he still sat below—then how could the Household vice minister, though concurrently grand counselor, sit above?

sentences.zh: 今散官自將仕郎至開府、特進，每品正、從有上中下，名級各異，則正從上下不得謂之同品。

translations.literal: Now among honorary officials, from Attendant Gentleman to Grand General Opening the Government and Special Advancement, each rank has upper, middle, and lower grades within the regular and lower series, and the titles and grades differ; therefore upper, lower, and middle within the regular and lower series cannot be called the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: Among honorary officials, from Attendant Gentleman to Grand General Opening the Government and Special Advancement, each rank has upper, middle, and lower grades within the regular and lower series, and the titles and grades differ; therefore upper, lower, and middle within a single rank cannot be treated as identical.

sentences.zh: 京兆、河南司錄及諸府州錄事參軍事皆操紀律，正諸曹，與尚書省左、右丞紀綱六曹略等，假使諸曹掾因功勞加台省官，安得位在司錄、錄事參軍上？

translations.literal: The recorders of the capital and Henan metropolitan prefectures and the recorders of the various prefectures and districts all wield disciplinary authority and regulate the various bureaus—roughly equal to the left and right vice directors who maintain order over the six bureaus in the Department of State Affairs; even if a bureau aide were rewarded with a concurrent Chancellery or Secretariat post for merit, how could he sit above the recorders?
translations.idiomatic: The recorders of the capital and Henan metropolitan prefectures and the recorders of the various prefectures and districts all wield disciplinary authority and regulate the various bureaus—roughly equal to the left and right vice directors who maintain order over the six bureaus in the Department of State Affairs; even if a bureau aide were rewarded with a concurrent Chancellery or Secretariat post for merit, how could he sit above the recorders?

sentences.zh: 且左丞糾射八坐，主省內禁令、宗廟祠祭事，御史不當，得彈奏之，良以台官所奏，拘牽成例，不揣事之輕重。

translations.literal: Moreover the left vice director investigates and impeaches the eight chief ministers, oversees internal prohibitions and ancestral temple wrongdoing, and when censors are improper may impeach them—precisely because censorate memorials are bound by precedent and do not weigh the gravity of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the left vice director investigates and impeaches the eight chief ministers, oversees internal prohibitions and ancestral temple sacrifices, and may impeach censors who act improperly—yet censorate memorials are bound by precedent and do not weigh the gravity of the matter.

sentences.zh: 使理可循，雖無往比，自宜行之。

translations.literal: If the principle can be followed, even without a past parallel it should be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: If the principle can be followed, even without a past parallel it should be implemented.

sentences.zh: 否者，號曰舊章，正可改也。

translations.literal: Otherwise, what is called an old statute may rightly be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, what is called an old statute may rightly be changed.

sentences.zh: 武宗詔兩省官詳議，皆從簡請。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong ordered officials of the two Chancelleries to discuss it in detail; all followed Jian's request.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong ordered officials of the two Chancelleries to discuss it in detail; all approved Jian's proposal.

sentences.zh: 曆河中、興元、宣武節度使，檢校尚書右僕射、東都留守。

translations.literal: He served in succession as military governor of Hedong, Xingyuan, and Xuanwu, and as acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as military governor of Hedong, Xingyuan, and Xuanwu, and as acting right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 而弟范亦為淄青節度使，世推顯家。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fan also became military governor of Ziqing; the world acclaimed them as a distinguished family.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fan also became military governor of Ziqing; the world acclaimed them as a distinguished family.

sentences.zh: 李白李白，字太白，興聖皇帝九世孫。

translations.literal: Li Bai—Li Bai, courtesy name Taibai, was ninth-generation descendant of Emperor Xingsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bai—Li Bai, courtesy name Taibai, was a ninth-generation descendant of Emperor Xingsheng.

sentences.zh: 其先隋末以罪徙西域，神龍初，遁還，客巴西。

translations.literal: His ancestors, at the end of Sui for a crime were banished to the Western Regions; in the early Shenlong period they fled back and sojourned in Brazil.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors, convicted of a crime at the end of the Sui, were banished to the Western Regions; in the early Shenlong period they fled back and settled as guests in Brazil.

sentences.zh: 白之生，母夢長庚星，因以命之。

translations.literal: When Bai was born, his mother dreamed of the Great Metal Star and therefore gave him that name.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai was born, his mother dreamed of the Great Metal Star and therefore gave him that name.

sentences.zh: 十歲通詩書，既長，隱岷山。

translations.literal: At ten he mastered poetry and the classics; when grown, he lived in seclusion on Mount Min.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he had mastered poetry and the classics; when grown, he lived in seclusion on Mount Min.

sentences.zh: 州舉有道，不應。

translations.literal: The prefecture nominated him for the "Way" examination; he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture nominated him for the Way examination; he did not respond.

sentences.zh: 蘇頲為益州長史，見白異之，曰：「是子天才英特，少益以學，可比相如。」

translations.literal: Su Ting was chief administrator of Yizhou; seeing Bai he regarded him as extraordinary and said: "This boy's talent is brilliant and singular; with a little more learning he could be compared to Sima Xiangru."
translations.idiomatic: When Su Ting was chief administrator of Yizhou, he saw Bai, regarded him as extraordinary, and said, "This boy's talent is brilliant and singular; with a little more learning he could rival Sima Xiangru.

sentences.zh: 然喜縱橫術，擊劍，為任俠，輕財重施。

translations.literal: Yet he delighted in the arts of vertical and horizontal alliance, swordplay, chivalrous deeds, and was light with wealth and generous in giving.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he delighted in the arts of vertical and horizontal alliance, swordplay, and chivalrous deeds, and was light with wealth and generous in giving.

sentences.zh: 更客任城，與孔巢父、韓准、裴政、張叔明、陶沔居徂徠山，日沈飲，號「竹溪六逸」。

translations.literal: He later sojourned at Rencheng; with Kong Chaofu, Han Zhun, Pei Zheng, Zhang Shuming, and Tao Mian he lived on Mount Culai, drinking deep every day—they were called the "Six Recluses of Bamboo Stream."
translations.idiomatic: He later sojourned at Rencheng; with Kong Chaofu, Han Zhun, Pei Zheng, Zhang Shuming, and Tao Mian he lived on Mount Culai, drinking deep every day—they were called the "Six Recluses of Bamboo Stream."

sentences.zh: 天寶初，南入會稽，與吳筠善，筠被召，故白亦至長安。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao period he went south to Kuaiji and became close with Wu Yun; when Yun was summoned to court, Bai therefore also went to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianbao period he went south to Kuaiji and became close with Wu Yun; when Yun was summoned to court, Bai therefore also went to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 往見賀知章，知章見其文，歎曰：「子，謫仙人也！」

translations.literal: He went to see He Zhizhang; Zhizhang read his writings and sighed: "You are an immortal banished to earth!
translations.idiomatic: He went to see He Zhizhang; Zhizhang read his writings and sighed, "You are an immortal banished to earth!

sentences.zh: 言于玄宗，召見金鑾殿，論當世事，奏頌一篇。

translations.literal: He spoke of this to Xuanzong, who summoned Bai to audience in the Hall of Golden Bells, discussed affairs of the time, and Bai presented a eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of this to Xuanzong, who summoned Bai to audience in the Hall of Golden Bells, discussed affairs of the time, and received a eulogy Bai presented.

sentences.zh: 帝賜食，親為調羹，有詔供奉翰林。

translations.literal: The Emperor granted him food and personally seasoned his broth; there was an edict appointing him to the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him food and personally seasoned his broth; an edict appointed him to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 白猶與飲徒醉於市。

translations.literal: Bai still drank with his companions and got drunk in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Bai still drank with his carousing companions and got drunk in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 帝坐沈香亭子，意有所感，欲得白為樂章；

translations.literal: The Emperor sat in the Pavilion of Agarwood, his mind stirred with feeling, and wished to have Bai compose a song-text;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sat in the Pavilion of Agarwood, his mind stirred with feeling, and wished to have Bai compose a song-text;

sentences.zh: 召入，而白已醉，左右以水靧面，稍解，援筆成文，婉麗精切無留思。

translations.literal: Bai was summoned in, but was already drunk; attendants splashed water on his face; when he sobered slightly he took brush and finished the piece—graceful, refined, and exact, without lingering thought.
translations.idiomatic: Bai was summoned in, but was already drunk; attendants splashed water on his face; when he sobered slightly he took up the brush and finished the piece—graceful, refined, and exact, without a moment's hesitation.

sentences.zh: 帝愛其才，數宴見。

translations.literal: The Emperor loved his talent and frequently feasted with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved his talent and frequently feasted with him.

sentences.zh: 白嘗侍帝，醉，使高力士脫靴。

translations.literal: Once when Bai was attending the Emperor while drunk, he ordered Gao Lishi to remove his boots.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Bai was attending the emperor while drunk, he ordered Gao Lishi to remove his boots.

sentences.zh: 力士素貴，恥之，擿其詩以激楊貴妃，帝欲官白，妃輒沮止。

translations.literal: Lishi had always been honored and felt shamed; he picked out lines from Bai's poems to provoke Yang Guifei; when the Emperor wished to grant Bai an office, the consort always blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi had always been honored and felt shamed; he picked out lines from Bai's poems to provoke Yang Guifei; when the emperor wished to grant Bai an office, the consort always blocked it.

sentences.zh: 白自知不為親近所容，益驁放不自脩，與知章、李適之、汝陽王璡、崔宗之、蘇晉、張旭、焦遂為「酒八仙人」。

translations.literal: Bai knew he was not tolerated by those close to the throne and grew ever more proud and unrestrained; with Zhizhang, Li Shizhi, Prince of Ruyang Li Jin, Cui Zongzhi, Su Jin, Zhang Xu, and Jiao Sui he was called the "Eight Immortals of the Wine Cup."
translations.idiomatic: Bai knew he was not tolerated by those close to the throne and grew ever more proud and unrestrained; with Zhizhang, Li Shizhi, Prince of Ruyang Li Jin, Cui Zongzhi, Su Jin, Zhang Xu, and Jiao Sui he was called the "Eight Immortals of the Wine Cup."

sentences.zh: 懇求還山，帝賜金放還。

translations.literal: He earnestly begged to return to the mountains; the Emperor granted him gold and released him.
translations.idiomatic: He earnestly begged to return to the mountains; the emperor granted him gold and released him.

sentences.zh: 白浮游四方，嘗乘舟與崔宗之自採石至金陵，著宮錦袍坐舟中，旁若無人。

translations.literal: Bai drifted through the four quarters; once he took a boat with Cui Zongzhi from Caishi to Jinling, wearing a palace brocade robe and sitting in the boat as if no one else were present.
translations.idiomatic: Bai drifted through the four quarters; once he took a boat with Cui Zongzhi from Caishi to Jinling, wearing a palace brocade robe and sitting in the boat as if no one else were present.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，轉側宿松、匡廬間，永王璘辟為府僚佐。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Bai wandered between Susong and Mount Lu; Prince of Yong Li Lin summoned him as a staff aide.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Bai wandered between Susong and Mount Lu; Prince of Yong Li Lin summoned him as a staff aide.

sentences.zh: 璘起兵，逃還彭澤，璘敗，當誅。

translations.literal: When Lin raised troops, Bai fled back to Pengze; when Lin was defeated, Bai was liable to execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin raised troops, Bai fled back to Pengze; when Lin was defeated, Bai was liable to execution.

sentences.zh: 初，白遊并州，見郭子儀，奇之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bai traveled in Bingzhou, he met Guo Ziyi and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Bai traveled in Bingzhou, he met Guo Ziyi and regarded him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 子儀嘗犯法，白為救免。

translations.literal: Ziyi once violated the law; Bai interceded and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi once violated the law; Bai interceded and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 至是子儀請解官以贖，有詔長流夜郎。

translations.literal: At this time Ziyi asked to resign his office to redeem Bai; an edict sentenced Bai to distant exile at Yelang.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Ziyi asked to resign his office to redeem Bai; an edict sentenced Bai to distant exile at Yelang.

sentences.zh: 會赦，還尋陽，坐事下獄。

translations.literal: When an amnesty was proclaimed he returned to Xunyang, but because of an offense was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty was proclaimed he returned to Xunyang, but because of an offense was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 時宋若思將吳兵三千赴河南，道尋陽，釋囚辟為參謀，未幾辭職。

translations.literal: At that time Song Ruosi was leading three thousand Wu troops south to Henan; passing Xunyang he released the prisoners and summoned Bai as strategist; before long Bai resigned the post.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Song Ruosi was leading three thousand Wu troops south to Henan; passing Xunyang he released the prisoners and summoned Bai as strategist; before long Bai resigned the post.

sentences.zh: 李陽冰為當塗令，白依之。

translations.literal: Li Yangbing was magistrate of Dangtu; Bai relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yangbing was magistrate of Dangtu; Bai relied on him.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，以左拾遺召，而白已卒，年六十餘。

translations.literal: When Daizong ascended the throne, Bai was summoned as Left Reminder, but Bai had already died, aged over sixty.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong ascended the throne, Bai was summoned as left reminder, but Bai had already died, aged over sixty.

sentences.zh: 白晚好黃老，度牛渚磯至姑孰，悅謝家青山，欲終焉。

translations.literal: In his later years Bai came to love the Yellow Emperor and Laozi; crossing Ox's Tail Ford to Gushu, he delighted in the Xie family's Green Mountain and wished to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Bai came to love the teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi; crossing Ox's Tail Ford to Gushu, he delighted in the Xie family's Green Mountain and wished to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 及卒，葬東麓。

translations.literal: When he died he was buried on the eastern slope.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was buried on the eastern slope.

sentences.zh: 元和末，宣歙觀察使范傳正祭其塚，禁樵採。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhe, Fan Chuanzheng, military governor of Xuan and She, sacrificed at his tomb and forbade woodcutting.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanhe, Fan Chuanzheng, military governor of Xuan and She, sacrificed at his tomb and forbade woodcutting.

sentences.zh: 訪後裔，惟二孫女嫁為民妻，進止仍有風範，因泣曰：「先祖志在青山，頃葬東麓，非本意。」

translations.literal: He sought descendants; only two granddaughters had married commoners; in bearing and deportment they still had distinction; he wept and said: "Our ancestor's wish was to lie on Green Mountain; he was recently buried on the eastern slope—not his true intent."
translations.idiomatic: He sought descendants; only two granddaughters had married commoners; in bearing and deportment they still had distinction; he wept and said, "Our ancestor's wish was to lie on Green Mountain; he was recently buried on the eastern slope—not his true intent.

sentences.zh: 傳正為改葬，立二碑焉。

translations.literal: Chuanzheng had him reburied and erected two steles.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanzheng had him reburied and erected two steles.

sentences.zh: 告二女，將改妻士族，辭以孤窮失身，命也，不願更嫁。

translations.literal: He told the two daughters he would arrange marriages for them with gentry families; they declined, saying that in loneliness and poverty they had lost their station—it was fate—and they did not wish to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: He told the two daughters he would arrange marriages for them with gentry families; they declined, saying that in loneliness and poverty they had lost their station—it was fate—and they did not wish to remarry.

sentences.zh: 傳正嘉歎，復其夫徭役。

translations.literal: Chuanzheng admired and sighed, and exempted their husbands from corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanzheng admired and sighed, and exempted their husbands from corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 文宗時，詔以白歌詩、裴旻劍舞、張旭草書為「三絕」。

translations.literal: In the Wenzong period an edict declared Bai's song-poetry, Pei Min's sword dance, and Zhang Xu's cursive script the "Three Unsurpassed Arts."
translations.idiomatic: In the Wenzong period an edict declared Bai's song-poetry, Pei Min's sword dance, and Zhang Xu's cursive script the "Three Unsurpassed Arts."

sentences.zh: 附 張旭旭，蘇州吳人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Zhang Xu—Xu was a man of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Zhang Xu—Xu was a man of Wu in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 嗜酒，每大醉，呼叫狂走，乃下筆，或以頭濡墨而書，既醒自視，以為神，不可復得也，世呼「張顛」。

translations.literal: He loved wine; whenever greatly drunk he would shout and run wildly, then take up the brush—or dip his head in ink and write; when sober he looked at what he had done and thought it divine, beyond recovery; the world called him "Zhang the Mad."
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine; whenever greatly drunk he would shout and run wildly, then take up the brush—or dip his head in ink and write; when sober he looked at what he had done and thought it divine, beyond recovery; the world called him "Zhang the Mad."

sentences.zh: 初，仕為常熟尉，有老人陳牒求判，宿昔又來，旭怒其煩，責之。

translations.literal: Earlier, in office as magistrate of Changshu, an old man submitted a petition seeking a judgment; he came again the next day; Xu, angered by the bother, rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving as magistrate of Changshu, an old man submitted a petition seeking a judgment; he came again the next day; Xu, angered by the bother, rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 老人曰：「觀公筆奇妙，欲以藏家爾。」

translations.literal: The old man said: "Observing your brushwork's marvel, I wished to keep it in my family."
translations.idiomatic: The old man said, "Observing the marvel of your brushwork, I wished to keep it in my family.

sentences.zh: 旭因問所藏，盡出其父書，旭視之，天下奇筆也，自是盡其法。

translations.literal: Xu therefore asked what he had collected and the man brought out all his father's writings; Xu looked at them—they were the finest brushwork under heaven; from then on he mastered the method entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Xu therefore asked what he had collected, and the man brought out all his father's writings; Xu looked at them—they were the finest brushwork under heaven; from then on he mastered the method entirely.

sentences.zh: 旭自言，始見公主擔夫爭道，又聞鼓吹，而得筆法意，觀倡公孫舞《劍器》，得其神。

translations.literal: Xu himself said that first seeing the princess's porters quarrel over the road, and then hearing the ceremonial music, he gained the intent of brush method; watching the courtesan Lady Gongsun dance the "Sword Brandisher," he gained its spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Xu himself said that first seeing the princess's porters quarrel over the road, and then hearing the ceremonial music, he gained the intent of brush method; watching the courtesan Lady Gongsun dance the "Sword Brandisher," he gained its spirit.

sentences.zh: 後人論書，歐、虞、褚、陸皆有異論，至旭，無非短者。

translations.literal: Later men discussing calligraphy had differing views on Ouyang Xun, Yu Shinan, Chu Suiliang, and Lu Jianzhi—but concerning Xu, none had anything but praise.
translations.idiomatic: Later men discussing calligraphy had differing views on Ouyang Xun, Yu Shinan, Chu Suiliang, and Lu Jianzhi—but concerning Xu, none had anything but praise.

sentences.zh: 傳其法，惟崔邈、顏真卿云。

translations.literal: Those who transmitted his method were only Cui Zao and Yan Zhenqing, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Those who transmitted his method were only Cui Zao and Yan Zhenqing, it is said.

sentences.zh: 附 裴旻旻嘗與幽州都督孫佺北伐，為奚所圍，旻舞刀立馬上，矢四集，皆迎刀而斷，奚大驚引去。

translations.literal: Appendix: Pei Min—Min once joined Youzhou governor Sun Chuo on a northern campaign; surrounded by the Xi, Min danced with his sword standing on horseback; four volleys of arrows converged and all were met and cut down by the blade; the Xi were greatly alarmed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Pei Min—Min once joined Youzhou governor Sun Chuo on a northern campaign; surrounded by the Xi, Min danced with his sword standing on horseback; four volleys of arrows converged and all were met and cut down by the blade; the Xi were greatly alarmed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後以龍華軍使守北平。

translations.literal: Later he served as Longhua Army commissioner defending Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Longhua Army commissioner defending Beiping.

sentences.zh: 北平多虎，旻善射，一日得虎三十一，休山下。

translations.literal: Beiping had many tigers; Min was skilled at archery; in one day he got thirty-one tigers below Rest Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Beiping had many tigers; Min was skilled at archery; in one day he got thirty-one tigers below Rest Mountain.

sentences.zh: 有老父曰：「此彪也。

translations.literal: An old man said: "These are cubs.
translations.idiomatic: An old man said, "These are cubs.

sentences.zh: 稍北，有真虎，使將軍遇之，且敗。」

translations.literal: A little farther north are real tigers; if the general meets them, he will be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: A little farther north are real tigers; if the general meets them, he will be defeated.

sentences.zh: 旻不信，怒馬趨之。

translations.literal: Min did not believe it and galloped angrily toward them.
translations.idiomatic: Min did not believe it and galloped angrily toward them.

sentences.zh: 有虎出叢薄中，小而猛，據地大吼，旻馬辟易，弓矢皆墮，自是不復射。

translations.literal: A tiger emerged from the thicket—small but fierce; crouching on the ground it roared greatly; Min's horse shied; bow and arrows all fell; from then on he never shot again.
translations.idiomatic: A tiger emerged from the thicket—small but fierce; crouching on the ground it roared greatly; Min's horse shied; bow and arrows all fell; from then on he never shot again.

sentences.zh: 王維王維，字摩詰。

translations.literal: Wang Wei—Wang Wei, courtesy name Mojie.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei—Wang Wei, courtesy name Mojie.

sentences.zh: 九歲知屬辭，與弟縉齊名，資孝友。

translations.literal: At nine he knew how to compose; he and his younger brother Jin were equally renowned, endowed with filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he knew how to compose; he and his younger brother Jin were equally renowned, endowed with filial piety and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 開元初，擢進士，調太樂丞，坐累為濟州司倉參軍。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan period he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Grand Music Director, and because of an offense was demoted to warehouse officer of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan period he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed grand music director, and because of an offense was demoted to warehouse officer of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 張九齡執政，擢右拾遺。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jiuling held power, Wei was promoted to Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jiuling held power, Wei was promoted to right reminder.

sentences.zh: 歷監察御史。

translations.literal: He served as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 母喪，毀幾不生。

translations.literal: When his mother died, his grief nearly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, his grief nearly killed him.

sentences.zh: 服除，累遷給事中。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was promoted in succession to Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was promoted in succession to gentleman attendant.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，玄宗西狩，維為賊得，以藥下利，陽喑。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Xuanzong went west on campaign; Wei was captured by the rebels; he took medicine to induce diarrhea and feigned muteness.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Xuanzong went west on campaign; Wei was captured by the rebels; he took medicine to induce diarrhea and feigned muteness.

sentences.zh: 祿山素知其才，迎置洛陽，迫為給事中。

translations.literal: Lushan had always known his talent and welcomed him to Luoyang, forcing him to serve as Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan had always known his talent and welcomed him to Luoyang, forcing him to serve as gentleman attendant.

sentences.zh: 祿山大宴凝碧池，悉召梨園諸工合樂，諸工皆泣，維聞悲甚，賦詩悼痛。

translations.literal: Lushan held a great feast at Ningbi Pool and summoned all the Pear Garden artisans to perform together; the artisans all wept; Wei heard and grieved deeply and composed a poem of mourning and pain.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan held a great feast at Ningbi Pool and summoned all the Pear Garden artisans to perform together; the artisans all wept; Wei heard and grieved deeply and composed a poem of mourning and pain.

sentences.zh: 賊平，皆下獄。

translations.literal: When the rebels were suppressed, all were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were suppressed, all were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 或以詩聞行在，時縉位已顯，請削官贖維罪，肅宗亦自憐之，下遷太子中允。

translations.literal: Some heard the poem at the imperial camp; at that time Jin's position was already prominent; he asked to strip his own rank to redeem Wei's crime; Suzong also pitied Wei and demoted him to palace attendant of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Some heard the poem at the imperial camp; at that time Jin's position was already prominent; he asked to strip his own rank to redeem Wei's crime; Suzong also pitied Wei and demoted him to palace attendant of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷中庶子，三遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to palace tutor, and three times promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was promoted to palace tutor, and in three promotions reached right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 縉為蜀州刺史未還，維自表「己有五短，縉五長，臣在省戶，縉遠方，願歸所任官，放田里，使縉得還京師。」

translations.literal: Jin was governor of Shu and had not yet returned; Wei submitted a memorial himself: "I have five shortcomings, Jin has five strengths; I am at the capital while Jin is far away; I wish to resign my current office and return to the fields, so that Jin may return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was governor of Shu and had not yet returned; Wei submitted a memorial himself: "I have five shortcomings, Jin has five strengths; I am at the capital while Jin is far away; I wish to resign my current office and return to the fields, so that Jin may return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 議者不之罪。

translations.literal: The critics did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial's critics did not fault him for it.

sentences.zh: 久乃召縉為左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: After a long time Jin was summoned as Left Regular Attendant of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Jin was summoned back to serve as left regular attendant of the palace.

sentences.zh: 上元初卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shangyuan era he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Shangyuan era, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 疾甚，縉在鳳翔，作書與別，又遺親故書數幅，停筆而化。

translations.literal: When his illness was severe, Jin was at Fengxiang; he wrote a letter of farewell, also left several letters to relatives and old friends, and passed away as he laid down his brush.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew grave, Jin was at Fengxiang. Wei wrote him a letter of farewell, then left several letters to relatives and old friends, and died the moment he set down his brush.

sentences.zh: 贈秘書監。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title of director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 維工草隸，善畫，名盛於開元、天寶間，豪英貴人虛左以迎，甯、薛諸王待若師友。

translations.literal: Wei was skilled in cursive and clerical script and good at painting; his fame flourished in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras; heroes and nobles left the seat of honor empty to receive him; the princes of Ning and Xue treated him as teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: Wei excelled at cursive and clerical calligraphy and was a gifted painter. His fame peaked during the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, when eminent men and nobles would leave the seat of honor vacant to receive him, and the Princes of Ning and Xue treated him as a teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 畫思入神，至山水準遠，雲勢石色，繪工以為天機所到，學者不及也。

translations.literal: His painting thoughts entered the divine; as for landscape, depth and distance, cloud momentum and rock color, painters held that where heavenly inspiration reached, learners could not attain.
translations.idiomatic: His painting was inspired to the point of genius. In landscape—depth, distance, the movement of clouds, the color of rock—painters said that where divine inspiration touched, students could not follow.

sentences.zh: 客有以《按樂圖》示者，無題識，維徐曰：「此《霓裳》第三疊最初拍也。」

translations.literal: A guest showed him the "Picture of Music Performance"; there was no title or inscription; Wei slowly said: "This is the opening beat of the third movement of the 'Rainbow Skirt'.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest showed him the *Picture of Music Performance*, which bore no title or inscription, Wei said slowly, "This is the opening beat of the third movement of the *Rainbow Skirt*.

sentences.zh: 客未然，引工按曲，乃信。

translations.literal: The guest was not yet convinced; he brought in a musician to perform the tune, and then believed.
translations.idiomatic: The guest was unconvinced until he brought in a musician to perform the piece, and then he believed.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆篤志奉佛，食不葷，衣不文彩。

translations.literal: The brothers all devoted their wills to Buddhism; they ate no meat and wore no patterned silk.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers were devout Buddhists: they ate no meat and wore no patterned silk.

sentences.zh: 別墅在輞川，地奇勝，有華子岡、欹湖、竹裏館、柳浪、茱萸沜、辛夷塢，與裴迪遊其中，賦詩相酬為樂。

translations.literal: Their villa was at Wangchuan, the land wondrous and surpassing, with Huazi Hill, Qi Lake, Bamboo Grove Lodge, Willow Waves, Dogwood Marsh, and Magnolia Cove; with Pei Di they roamed there, composing poems in reply to each other for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Their villa at Wangchuan lay in country of rare beauty—Huazi Hill, Qi Lake, Bamboo Grove Lodge, Willow Waves, Dogwood Marsh, Magnolia Cove—and there Wei wandered with Pei Di, exchanging poems for their delight.

sentences.zh: 喪妻不娶，孤居三十年。

translations.literal: After his wife's death he did not remarry, living alone for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: After his wife died he never remarried, living alone for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 母亡，表輞川第為寺，終葬其西。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he petitioned to make the Wangchuan residence a temple and was finally buried to its west.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he petitioned to convert the Wangchuan estate into a temple, and was himself buried west of it at the end.

sentences.zh: 寶應中，代宗語縉曰：「朕嘗于諸王座聞維樂章，今傳幾何？」

translations.literal: In the Baoying era, Emperor Daizong said to Jin: "I once heard Wei's musical compositions among the princes; how many are transmitted now?
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoying era, Emperor Daizong said to Jin, "I once heard Wang Wei's songs among the princes. How many of them survive today?

sentences.zh: 遣中人王承華往取，縉裒集數十百篇上之。

translations.literal: He sent the eunuch Wang Chenghua to fetch them; Jin collected several tens or hundreds of pieces and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the eunuch Wang Chenghua to collect them, and Jin gathered several dozen or hundred pieces and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 鄭虔鄭虔，鄭州滎陽人。

translations.literal: Zheng Qian—Zheng Qian was a native of Xingyang in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qian, a native of Xingyang in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，為協律郎，集綴當世事，著書八十餘篇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he served as Coordinator of Music; he collected and arranged current affairs and wrote more than eighty chapters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he served as coordinator of music, gathering and arranging accounts of current affairs into a work of more than eighty chapters.

sentences.zh: 有窺其稿者，上書告虔私撰國史，虔蒼黃焚之，坐謫十年。

translations.literal: Someone who had peeked at his draft submitted a memorial accusing Qian of privately compiling a national history; Qian in panic burned it and was punished by exile for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Someone who had glimpsed his draft reported that Qian was privately compiling a national history. Qian burned the manuscript in panic and was sentenced to ten years' exile.

sentences.zh: 還京師，玄宗愛其才，欲置左右，以不事事，更為置廣文館，以虔為博士。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, Xuanzong loved his talent and wished to place him at his side; because he did not attend to routine affairs, he instead established the Broad Culture Hall and made Qian its academician.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital, Xuanzong admired his talent and wanted him at court, but because Qian was no hand at routine administration, the emperor instead established the Broad Culture Hall and appointed him its academician.

sentences.zh: 虔聞命，不知廣文曹司何在，訴宰相，宰相曰：「上增國學，置廣文館，以居賢者，令後世言廣文博士自君始，不亦美乎？」

translations.literal: Qian received the appointment and did not know where the Broad Culture office was; he appealed to the chief minister, who said: "The emperor expanded the National University and established the Broad Culture Hall to house men of talent. That later ages should say the Broad Culture academician began with you—is that not fine?
translations.idiomatic: On receiving the appointment, Qian did not even know where the Broad Culture office was and appealed to the chief minister, who said, "The emperor expanded the National University and established the Broad Culture Hall to house men of talent. That posterity should say the Broad Culture academician began with you—is that not an honor?

sentences.zh: 虔乃就職。

translations.literal: Qian then took up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Qian then took up the post.

sentences.zh: 久之，雨壞廡舍，有司不復修完，寓治國子館，自是遂廢。

translations.literal: After a long time rain ruined the corridor buildings; the responsible office did not repair them; they were lodged in the Directorate of Education, and from then on the hall fell into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: In time rain destroyed the corridor buildings, and the authorities never repaired them. The hall was temporarily housed in the Directorate of Education, and thereafter fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 初，虔追紬故書可志者得四十餘篇，國子司業蘇源明名其書為《會稡》。

translations.literal: At first Qian, by searching old books for what was worth recording, obtained more than forty chapters; Su Yuanming, vice director of the Directorate of Education, named the book *Collected Records*.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, by combing through old books for material worth preserving, Qian had recovered more than forty chapters; Su Yuanming, vice director of the Directorate of Education, gave the work the title *Collected Records*.

sentences.zh: 虔善圖山水，好書，常苦無紙，於是慈恩寺貯柿葉數屋，遂往日取葉肄書，歲久殆遍。

translations.literal: Qian was good at landscape painting and loved writing; he often suffered from lack of paper; thus at Cien Temple he stored persimmon leaves in several rooms and went daily to take leaves to practice writing; over the years he nearly covered them all.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was skilled at landscape painting and loved to write, but often lacked paper. At Cien Temple he therefore stored persimmon leaves in several rooms and went each day to gather leaves for practice; over the years he had nearly covered them all.

sentences.zh: 嘗自寫其詩並畫以獻，帝大署其尾曰：「鄭虔三絕」。

translations.literal: Once he copied his own poems together with a painting and presented them; the emperor wrote large characters at the end saying "Zheng Qian's Three Perfections."
translations.idiomatic: Once he presented copies of his own poems together with a painting, and the emperor wrote in large characters at the end, "Zheng Qian's Three Perfections."

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Drafting Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafting gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，遣張通儒劫百官置東都，偽授虔水部郎中，因稱風緩，求攝市令，潛以密章達靈武。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he sent Zhang Tongru to seize the officials and place them in the Eastern Capital; Qian was falsely appointed Director in the Ministry of Works; he then claimed wind paralysis, sought appointment as acting market magistrate, and secretly sent a confidential memorial to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he sent Zhang Tongru to seize the officials and hold them in the Eastern Capital. Qian was given a false appointment as director in the Ministry of Works; he then claimed to suffer from wind paralysis, sought a post as acting market magistrate, and secretly sent a confidential memorial to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 賊平，與張通、王維並囚宣陽裏。

translations.literal: When the rebels were suppressed, he was imprisoned together with Zhang Tong and Wang Wei in Xuanyang Lane.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was suppressed, he was imprisoned with Zhang Tong and Wang Wei in Xuanyang Lane.

sentences.zh: 三人者，皆善畫，崔圓使繪齋壁，虔等方悸死，即極思祈解於圓，卒免死，貶台州司戶參軍事，維止下選。

translations.literal: The three were all skilled at painting; Cui Yuan had them paint the walls of his study; Qian and the others, just then fearing death, exerted their utmost thought to beg release from Yuan and finally escaped death; Qian was demoted to assistant registrar of Taizhou, while Wei was merely removed from the selection rolls.
translations.idiomatic: All three were skilled painters. Cui Yuan had them paint the walls of his study; terrified of death, they poured every ounce of talent into pleading for release, and at last escaped execution. Qian was demoted to assistant registrar of Taizhou, while Wei was merely struck from the selection rolls.

sentences.zh: 後數年卒。

translations.literal: Several years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died several years later.

sentences.zh: 虔學長于地理，山川險易、方隅物產、兵戍眾寡無不詳。

translations.literal: Qian's learning excelled in geography; the peril and ease of mountains and rivers, regional products, and the numbers of garrisons and troops—none were not known in detail.
