translations.idiomatic: Qian's learning excelled in geography: the hazards and routes of mountains and rivers, regional products, and the strength of garrisons—none escaped his detailed knowledge.

sentences.zh: 嘗為《天寶軍防錄》，言典事該。

translations.literal: He once compiled the *Tianbao Record of Military Defenses*; its statements on canonical matters were comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled the *Tianbao Record of Military Defenses*, a work comprehensive in its treatment of institutional matters.

sentences.zh: 諸儒服其善著書，時號「鄭廣文」。

translations.literal: The scholars admired his skill in writing and at the time called him "Broad Culture Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars admired his gift for writing, and at the time he was known as "Broad Culture Zheng."

sentences.zh: 在官貧約甚，澹如也。

translations.literal: In office he was extremely poor and frugal, tranquil as if unconcerned.
translations.idiomatic: In office he lived in extreme poverty and frugality, serene and untroubled.

sentences.zh: 杜甫嘗贈以詩曰「才名四十年，坐客寒無氈」云。

translations.literal: Du Fu once presented him a poem saying "Forty years of talent and fame, yet guests sit shivering with no felt on the floor."
translations.idiomatic: Du Fu once wrote him a poem saying, "Forty years of talent and fame, yet guests sit shivering with no felt on the floor."

sentences.zh: 有鄭相如者，自滄州來，師事虔，虔未之禮，間問何所業，相如曰：「聞孔子稱'繼周者百世可知'，僕亦能知之。」

translations.literal: There was a Zheng Xiangru who came from Cangzhou to study under Qian as master; Qian did not treat him with courtesy; he casually asked what his pursuit was; Xiangru said: "I have heard Confucius say, 'He who succeeds the Zhou—his rule may be known a hundred generations hence'; I too can know this.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Zheng Xiangru came from Cangzhou to study under Qian, but Qian did not treat him with courtesy and casually asked what he pursued. Xiangru replied, "I have heard Confucius say, 'He who succeeds the Zhou—his rule may be known a hundred generations hence.' I too can know this.

sentences.zh: 虔駭然，即曰：「開元盡三十年當改元，盡十五年天下亂，賊臣僭位，公當汙偽官，願守節，可以免。」

translations.literal: Qian was startled and immediately said: "When the Kaiyuan era reaches thirty years the reign title will change; when fifteen more years pass the realm will fall into chaos; treacherous ministers will usurp rank; you will be stained with a false office—if you wish to keep your integrity, you may escape."
translations.idiomatic: Qian was startled and said at once, "When the Kaiyuan era reaches thirty years the reign title will change; fifteen years after that the realm will fall into chaos and treacherous ministers will usurp power. You will be forced into a false office—if you wish to preserve your integrity, you may yet escape."

sentences.zh: 虔又問：「自謂云何？」

translations.literal: Qian asked again: "What do you say of yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Qian asked again, "And what of your own fate?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「相如有官三年，死衢州。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Xiangru will hold office three years and die in Quzhou."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Xiangru will hold office for three years and die in Quzhou."

sentences.zh: 是年及進士第，調信安尉。

translations.literal: That year he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as assistant magistrate of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 既三年，虔詢吏部，則相如果死。

translations.literal: After three years Qian inquired at the Ministry of Personnel, and Xiangru had indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Qian inquired at the Ministry of Personnel and learned that Xiangru had indeed died.

sentences.zh: 故虔念其言，終不附賊。

translations.literal: Therefore Qian kept his words in mind and to the end did not attach himself to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Qian therefore kept his words in mind and never joined the rebels.

sentences.zh: 蕭穎士蕭穎士，字茂挺，梁鄱陽王恢七世孫。

translations.literal: Xiao Yingshi—Xiao Yingshi, courtesy name Maoting, was seventh-generation descendant of Prince Hui of Poyang of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingshi, whose courtesy name was Maoting, was a seventh-generation descendant of Prince Hui of Poyang of Liang.

sentences.zh: 祖晶，賢而有謀，任雅相伐高麗，表為記室。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jing was worthy and resourceful; when Ren Yaxiang campaigned against Goguryeo, he recommended him as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jing was a man of talent and strategy; when Ren Yaxiang campaigned against Goguryeo, he recommended him as recorder.

sentences.zh: 越王貞舉兵，杖策詣之，陳三策，王不用，晶度必敗，乃亡去，客死廣陵。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhen of Yue raised troops, Jing went with staff in hand to visit him, set forth three strategies; the prince did not adopt them; Jing judged he would surely fail, then fled and died as a guest in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhen of Yue raised troops, Jing went to him with staff in hand and offered three strategies. The prince ignored them; Jing foresaw defeat, fled, and died as a guest in Guangling.

sentences.zh: 穎士四歲屬文，十歲補太學生。

translations.literal: At four years Yingshi composed prose; at ten he entered the Imperial Academy as a student.
translations.idiomatic: Yingshi was composing prose at four and entered the Imperial Academy at ten.

sentences.zh: 觀書一覽即誦，通百家譜系、書籀學。

translations.literal: Reading a book once, he could recite it; he mastered the genealogies of the hundred schools and the study of ancient script.
translations.idiomatic: He could read a book once and recite it from memory, and mastered the genealogies of the hundred schools and the study of ancient script.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年，舉進士，對策第一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan he passed the jinshi examination and ranked first in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan he passed the jinshi examination and ranked first in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 父旻，以莒丞抵罪，穎士往訴于府佐張惟一，惟一曰：「旻有佳兒，吾以旻獲譴不憾。」

translations.literal: His father Min, as assistant magistrate of Ju, was charged with an offense; Yingshi went to plead before the prefectural aide Zhang Weiyi; Weiyi said: "Min has an excellent son; I do not regret being punished on Min's account.
translations.idiomatic: His father Min, assistant magistrate of Ju, was charged with an offense. Yingshi went to plead before the prefectural aide Zhang Weiyi, who said, "Min has an excellent son; I do not regret being punished on his account.

sentences.zh: 乃平宥之。

translations.literal: He then fully pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyi then fully pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，穎士補秘書正字。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, Yingshi was appointed proofreader of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era, Yingshi was appointed proofreader of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 于時裴耀卿、席豫、張均、宋遙、韋述皆先進，器其材，與鈞禮，由是名播天下。

translations.literal: At that time Pei Yaoging, Xi Yu, Zhang Jun, Song Yao, and Wei Shu were all senior figures; they valued his talent and treated him as an equal; thereby his name spread throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Yaoging, Xi Yu, Zhang Jun, Song Yao, and Wei Shu were all senior figures who valued his talent and treated him as an equal, and his name spread throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 奉使括遺書趙、衛間，淹久不報，為有司劾免，留客濮陽。

translations.literal: Sent on a mission to gather lost books between Zhao and Wei, he lingered long without reporting; he was impeached and dismissed by the responsible office and stayed as a guest in Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sent on a mission to gather lost books in the Zhao and Wei region, he lingered long without reporting back and was impeached and dismissed. He remained in Puyang as a guest.

sentences.zh: 於是尹征、王恒、盧異、盧士式、賈邕、趙匡、閻士和、柳並等皆執弟子禮，以次授業，號蕭夫子。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yin Zheng, Wang Heng, Lu Yi, Lu Shishi, Jia Yong, Zhao Kuang, Yan Shihe, Liu Bing, and others all observed the disciple's rite, receiving instruction in turn, and called him Master Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: There Yin Zheng, Wang Heng, Lu Yi, Lu Shishi, Jia Yong, Zhao Kuang, Yan Shihe, Liu Bing, and others all observed the rites of disciples, taking instruction from him in turn, and called him Master Xiao.

sentences.zh: 召為集賢校理。

translations.literal: He was summoned as collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 宰相李林甫欲見之，穎士方父喪，不詣。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Linfu wished to see him; Yingshi was in mourning for his father and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Linfu wished to see him, but Yingshi was in mourning for his father and did not go.

sentences.zh: 林甫嘗至故人舍邀潁士，穎士前往，哭門內以待，林甫不得已，前吊乃去。

translations.literal: Linfu once went to an old friend's house to invite Yingshi; Yingshi went ahead and waited inside the gate in mourning cries; Linfu had no choice but to go forward and offer condolences before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu once went to an old friend's house to summon Yingshi. Yingshi arrived first and waited inside the gate, wailing in mourning. Linfu had no choice but to enter and offer condolences before leaving.

sentences.zh: 怒其不下己，調廣陵參軍事，穎士急中不能堪，作《伐櫻桃樹賦》曰：「擢無庸之瑣質，蒙本枝以自庇。

translations.literal: Angry that he would not defer to him, he transferred him to military adjutant of Guangling; Yingshi, in distress, could not bear it and wrote the "Rhapsody on Felling the Cherry Tree," saying: "Raised for its worthless petty substance, sheltered by the main branch for its own protection.
translations.idiomatic: Angry that Yingshi would not defer to him, Linfu transferred him to military adjutant of Guangling. Yingshi, in distress, could not bear it and wrote the *Rhapsody on Felling the Cherry Tree*, saying, "Raised for its worthless petty substance, sheltered by the main branch for its own protection.

sentences.zh: 雖先寢而或薦，非和羹之正味。」

translations.literal: Though first put to bed it may sometimes be offered, it is not the proper flavor for harmonizing the stew.
translations.idiomatic: Though it may sometimes be served, it is not the proper flavor for harmonizing the stew.

sentences.zh: 以譏林甫雲。

translations.literal: To satirize Linfu, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: —a satire aimed at Linfu.

sentences.zh: 君子恨其褊。

translations.literal: Men of worth regretted his narrowness.
translations.idiomatic: Men of worth regretted his pettiness.

sentences.zh: 會母喪免，流播吳、越。

translations.literal: When his mother's mourning ended he was dismissed and wandered through Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother's mourning ended he was dismissed and wandered through Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂：「仲尼作《春秋》，為百王不易法，而司馬遷作本紀、書、表、世家、列傳，敘事依違，失褒貶體，不足以訓。」

translations.literal: He once said: "Confucius wrote the *Spring and Autumn Annals* as the unchanging law for a hundred kings, yet Sima Qian wrote Basic Annals, Treatises, Tables, Hereditary Houses, and Biographies; in narrating events he was irresolute and lost the body of praise and blame—it is insufficient for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Confucius wrote the *Spring and Autumn Annals* as the unchanging law for a hundred kings, yet Sima Qian's Basic Annals, Treatises, Tables, Hereditary Houses, and Biographies narrate events irresolutely and lose the body of praise and blame—they are insufficient for instruction.

sentences.zh: 乃起漢元年訖隋義寧編年，依《春秋》義類為傳百篇。

translations.literal: He therefore began from the first year of Han and ended at the Yining era of Sui, arranging by year and following the categories of meaning in the *Spring and Autumn* to make a history of a hundred chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore compiled a chronicle from the first year of Han down to the Yining era of Sui, arranging events by year and following the categories of the *Spring and Autumn* in a history of a hundred chapters.

sentences.zh: 在魏書高貴崩，曰：「司馬昭弑帝于南闕。」

translations.literal: In the Wei section, when Emperor Gaogui died, he wrote: "Sima Zhao assassinated the emperor at the Southern Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In his account of Wei, when Emperor Gaogui died, he wrote, "Sima Zhao assassinated the emperor at the Southern Gate.

sentences.zh: 在梁書陳受禪，曰：「陳霸先反。」

translations.literal: In the Liang section, when Chen received the abdication, he wrote: "Chen Baxian rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: In his account of Liang, when Chen received the abdication, he wrote, "Chen Baxian rebelled."

sentences.zh: 又自以梁枝孫，而宣帝逆取順守，故武帝得血食三紀；

translations.literal: Also, considering himself a collateral descendant of the Liang line, and that Emperor Xuan had seized power by irregular means yet maintained rule with orthodox rectitude, therefore Emperor Wu received blood sacrifices for three reigns;
translations.idiomatic: Also, as a collateral descendant of the Liang line, he held that Emperor Xuan had usurped the throne yet governed with orthodox rectitude—therefore Emperor Wu of Liang deserved sacrificial offerings across three reigns;

sentences.zh: 昔曲沃篡晉，而文公為五伯，仲尼弗貶也。

translations.literal: In old times Quwo usurped Jin, yet Duke Wen became one of the Five Hegemons, and Confucius did not demean him.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Quwo usurped Jin, yet Duke Wen became one of the Five Hegemons, and Confucius did not demean him.

sentences.zh: 乃黜陳閏隋，以唐土德承梁火德，皆自斷，諸儒不與論也。

translations.literal: He then rejected Chen and relegated Sui, holding that Tang's earth virtue succeeded Liang's fire virtue—all his own judgments, with which the scholars did not debate.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore rejected Chen and relegated Sui, holding that Tang's earth virtue succeeded Liang's fire virtue—all his own judgments, which the other scholars did not debate.

sentences.zh: 有太原王緒者，僧辯裔孫，撰《永甯公輔梁書》，黜陳不帝，穎士佐之，亦著《梁蕭史譜》及作《梁不禪陳論》以發緒義例，使光明雲。

translations.literal: There was a Wang Xu of Taiyuan, descendant of Wang Sengbian, who compiled the *History of Liang Assisting the Prince of Yongning*, rejecting Chen as imperial; Yingshi assisted him, also wrote the *Genealogical History of the Liang Xiao* and composed *On Liang's Refusal to Abdicate to Chen* to develop Xu's principles of historiography, making them clear and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Wang Xu of Taiyuan, a descendant of Wang Sengbian, who compiled the *History of Liang Assisting the Prince of Yongning*, rejecting Chen as a legitimate dynasty. Yingshi assisted him, also wrote the *Genealogical History of the Liang Xiao* and composed *On Liang's Refusal to Abdicate to Chen* to develop Xu's historiographical principles and bring them to clear light.

sentences.zh: 史官韋述薦穎士自代，召詣史館待制，穎士乘傳詣京師。

translations.literal: Historiographer Wei Shu recommended Yingshi to replace him; he was summoned to the History Office as awaiting orders; Yingshi traveled by post to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Historiographer Wei Shu recommended Yingshi to succeed him, and Yingshi was summoned to the History Office as awaiting orders. He traveled by post relay to the capital.

sentences.zh: 而林甫方威福自擅，穎士遂不屈，愈見疾，俄免官，往來鄠、杜間。

translations.literal: But Linfu was then monopolizing power and authority; Yingshi would not submit; he grew ever more hated, and soon was dismissed from office, passing back and forth between E and Du.
translations.idiomatic: But Linfu was then monopolizing power; Yingshi would not submit, grew ever more resented, and was soon dismissed, passing back and forth between E and Du.

sentences.zh: 林甫死，更調河南府參軍事。

translations.literal: When Linfu died, he was reassigned as military adjutant of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Linfu died, he was reassigned as military adjutant of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 倭國遣使入朝，自陳國人願得蕭夫子為師者，中書舍人張漸等諫不可而止。

translations.literal: Wa sent an envoy to court who stated that his countrymen wished to have Master Xiao as teacher; Zhang Jian and others, remonstrating ministers, said it could not be done, and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wa sent an envoy to court stating that his countrymen wished Master Xiao as their teacher, but Remonstrance Secretariat officials Zhang Jian and others argued against it, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 安祿山寵恣，穎士陰語柳並曰：「胡人負寵而驕，亂不久矣。

translations.literal: An Lushan was favored and unrestrained; Yingshi secretly said to Liu Bing: "The barbarian, bearing favor, is arrogant; chaos will not be long.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan was favored and unrestrained. Yingshi said privately to Liu Bing, "The barbarian, swollen with favor, grows arrogant—chaos will not be long in coming.

sentences.zh: 東京其先陷乎！」

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital will probably fall first!
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital will probably fall first!

sentences.zh: 即托疾遊太室山。

translations.literal: He then pleaded illness and traveled Mount Taishi.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded illness and traveled to Mount Taishi.

sentences.zh: 已而祿山反，穎士往見河南採訪使郭納，言禦守計，納忽不用，歎曰：「肉食者以兒戲禦劇賊，難矣哉！」

translations.literal: Before long Lushan rebelled; Yingshi went to see Henan Investigation Commissioner Guo Na and spoke of plans for defense; Na suddenly did not adopt them; he sighed and said: "Those who eat meat treat a fierce rebel as child's play—hard indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lushan rebelled. Yingshi went to see Henan investigation commissioner Guo Na and offered plans for defense, but Na abruptly ignored them. Yingshi sighed, "Those who eat meat treat a fierce rebel as child's play—hard indeed!

sentences.zh: 聞封常清陳兵東京，往觀之，不宿而還。

translations.literal: Hearing that Feng Changqing had deployed troops at the Eastern Capital, he went to observe; he did not stay overnight and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Feng Changqing had deployed troops at the Eastern Capital, he went to observe the situation but did not stay overnight and returned.

sentences.zh: 因藏家書於箕、穎間，身走山南，節度使源洧辟掌書記。

translations.literal: He therefore hid his family books between Ji and Ying, went in person to Shannan, and was recruited by Military Commissioner Yuan Wei as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He hid his family books in the Ji and Ying region, went in person to Shannan, and was recruited by military commissioner Yuan Wei as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 賊別校攻南陽，洧懼，欲退保江陵，穎士說曰：「官兵守潼關，財用急，必待江、淮轉餉乃足，餉道由漢、沔，則襄陽乃今天下喉襟，一日不守，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: A rebel detachment attacked Nanyang; Wei was afraid and wished to withdraw and hold Jiangling; Yingshi urged saying: "The government troops hold Tong Pass; finances are urgent; they must wait for grain transport from the Jiang and Huai before it is sufficient; the supply route goes through Han and Mian—then Xiangyang is today the throat and breast of the realm; one day not held, and the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: When a rebel detachment attacked Nanyang, Wei feared defeat and wished to withdraw to Jiangling. Yingshi urged him, "Government troops hold Tong Pass, but finances are desperate—they must wait for grain from the Jiang and Huai before supplies suffice. The supply route runs through Han and Mian, and Xiangyang is the throat of the realm today. Hold it one day less, and the great cause is lost.

sentences.zh: 且列郡數十，人百萬，訓兵攘寇，社稷之功也。

translations.literal: Moreover there are several dozen commanderies and a million people—training troops and repelling bandits is merit for the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, dozens of commanderies and a million people look to you—training troops and repelling bandits would be service to the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 賊方專崤、陝，公何遽輕土地，欲取笑天下乎？」

translations.literal: The rebels are now focused on Xiao and Shan—why do you so hastily treat the land lightly and wish to make yourself a laughingstock to the realm?
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are now focused on Xiao and Shan—why do you so hastily abandon this land and make yourself a laughingstock to the realm?

sentences.zh: 洧乃按甲不出。

translations.literal: Wei then held his troops and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Wei then held his troops and did not march out.

sentences.zh: 亦會祿山死，賊解去。

translations.literal: It also happened that Lushan died and the rebels dispersed and left.
translations.idiomatic: It also happened that Lushan died and the rebels dispersed.

sentences.zh: 洧卒，往客金陵，永王璘召之，不見。

translations.literal: When Wei died, he went as guest to Jinling; Prince Yong Li Lin summoned him, and he did not appear.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei died, he went to Jinling as a guest. Prince Yong Li Lin summoned him, but he did not appear.

sentences.zh: 時盛王為淮南節度大使，留蜀不遣，副大使李承式玩兵不振。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Sheng was Huainan military commissioner-in-chief, detained in Shu and not sent out; Vice Commissioner Li Chengshi played with troops and did not rouse them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Sheng was Huainan military commissioner-in-chief but was detained in Shu and not sent out; vice commissioner Li Chengshi dawdled with his troops and failed to rouse them.

sentences.zh: 穎士與宰相崔圓書，以為：「今兵食所資在東南，但楚、越重山復江，自古中原擾則盜先起，宜時遣王以捍鎮江淮。」

translations.literal: Yingshi wrote to Chief Minister Cui Yuan, holding that: "Now the resources of troops and grain lie in the southeast; but Chu and Yue have layered mountains and winding rivers; from antiquity when the central plains were disturbed, bandits rose first—the prince should be sent in timely fashion to defend and secure the Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Yingshi wrote to chief minister Cui Yuan, arguing, "The resources of troops and grain now lie in the southeast, but Chu and Yue are a maze of mountains and rivers—from antiquity, when the central plains were disturbed, bandits rose first. The prince should be sent at once to defend the Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 俄而劉展果反。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Zhan indeed rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu Zhan indeed rebelled.

sentences.zh: 賊圍雍丘，脅泗上軍，承式遣兵往救，大宴賓客，陳女樂。

translations.literal: Rebels besieged Yongqiu and threatened the Si River army; Chengshi sent troops to rescue and held a great feast for guests, displaying female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels besieged Yongqiu and threatened the Si River army. Chengshi sent troops to the rescue but held a great feast for his guests with female musicians on display.

sentences.zh: 穎士曰：「天子暴露，豈臣下盡歡時邪？

translations.literal: Yingshi said: "The Son of Heaven is exposed to the elements—is this the time for ministers and subordinates to revel to the full?
translations.idiomatic: Yingshi said, "The Son of Heaven is exposed to wind and rain—is this a time for ministers to revel to their hearts' content?

sentences.zh: 夫投兵不測，乃使觀聽華麗，一旦思歸，誰致其死哉？」

translations.literal: To commit troops to the uncertain, yet make them watch and listen to splendor—once they think of returning home, who will give their lives?
translations.idiomatic: You commit troops to an uncertain battle yet parade splendor before them—once they think of home, who will give their lives?

sentences.zh: 弗納。

translations.literal: He did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi did not listen.

sentences.zh: 崔圓聞之，即授揚州功曹參軍。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan heard of this and immediately appointed him Assistant Administrator of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Yuan heard of this, he immediately appointed Yingshi assistant administrator of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 至官，信宿去。

translations.literal: On reaching office, after one or two nights he left.
translations.idiomatic: He reached office, stayed one or two nights, and left.

sentences.zh: 後客死汝南逆旅，年五十二，門人共諡曰文元先生。

translations.literal: Later he died as a guest in an inn in Runan, aged fifty-two; his disciples together gave the posthumous title Master Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He later died as a guest in an inn in Runan, aged fifty-two. His disciples together gave him the posthumous title Master Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 穎士樂聞人善，以推引後進為己任，如李陽、李幼卿、皇甫冉、陸渭等數十人，由獎目，皆為名士。

translations.literal: Yingshi delighted in hearing of others' excellence and took recommending the young as his own task; such as Li Yang, Li Youqing, Huangfu Ran, Lu Wei, and several dozen others—through his praise and notice—all became eminent men.
translations.idiomatic: Yingshi delighted in hearing of others' excellence and made recommending the young his mission. Li Yang, Li Youqing, Huangfu Ran, Lu Wei, and several dozen others—all through his praise and notice—became eminent men.

sentences.zh: 天下推知人，稱蕭功曹。

translations.literal: The realm acclaimed his discernment of men and called him Assistant Administrator Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: The realm acclaimed his gift for discerning talent and called him Assistant Administrator Xiao.

sentences.zh: 嘗兄事元德秀，而友殷寅、顏真卿、柳芳、陸據、李華、邵軫、趙驊，時人語曰「殷、顏、柳、陸，李、蕭、邵、趙」，以能全其交也。

translations.literal: He once treated Yuan Dexiu as an elder brother, and was friends with Yin Yin, Yan Zhenqing, Liu Fang, Lu Ju, Li Hua, Shao Zhen, and Zhao Hua; people of the time said "Yin, Yan, Liu, Lu; Li, Xiao, Shao, Zhao"—because they could preserve their friendship intact.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Yuan Dexiu as an elder brother and was friends with Yin Yin, Yan Zhenqing, Liu Fang, Lu Ju, Li Hua, Shao Zhen, and Zhao Hua. People of the time said, "Yin, Yan, Liu, Lu; Li, Xiao, Shao, Zhao"—because they preserved their friendships intact.

sentences.zh: 所與游者，孔至、賈至、源行恭、張有略、族弟季遐、劉穎、韓拯、陳晉、孫益、韋建、韋收。

translations.literal: Those with whom he associated included Kong Zhi, Jia Zhi, Yuan Xinggong, Zhang Youlue, clansman cousin Ji Xia, Liu Ying, Han Zheng, Chen Jin, Sun Yi, Wei Jian, and Wei Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Those with whom he associated included Kong Zhi, Jia Zhi, Yuan Xinggong, Zhang Youlue, his clansman cousin Ji Xia, Liu Ying, Han Zheng, Chen Jin, Sun Yi, Wei Jian, and Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 獨華與齊名，世號「蕭、李」。

translations.literal: Only Hua was equally famous with him; the age called them "Xiao and Li."
translations.idiomatic: Only Li Hua matched his renown; their contemporaries called them "Xiao and Li."

sentences.zh: 嘗與華、據游洛龍門，讀路旁碑，穎士即誦，華再閱，據三乃能盡記。

translations.literal: Once, together with Hua and Ju, he visited Longmen at Luoyang, read a roadside stele, and Yingshi recited it at once; Hua after two readings, and Ju only after three could fully memorize it.
translations.idiomatic: Once he visited Longmen at Luoyang with Li Hua and Lu Ju. They read a roadside stele: Yingshi recited it immediately, Hua after two readings, and Ju only after three could commit it entirely to memory.

sentences.zh: 聞者謂三人才高下，此其分也。

translations.literal: Those who heard of it said that among the three men's talents high and low, this was the dividing mark.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard of it said this episode showed exactly where the three men's talents ranked.

sentences.zh: 有奴事穎士十年，笞楚嚴慘，或勸其去，答曰：「非不能，愛其才耳。」

translations.literal: There was a servant who attended Yingshi for ten years; the flogging was severe and cruel. Some urged him to leave, and he answered: "It is not that I cannot; I love his talent, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: A servant had attended Yingshi for ten years under severe and cruel beatings. When some urged him to leave, he replied, "It is not that I cannot—I simply love his talent.

sentences.zh: 穎士數稱班彪、皇甫謐、張華、劉琨、潘尼能尚古，而混流俗不自振，曹植、陸機所不逮也；

translations.literal: Yingshi often praised Ban Biao, Huangfu Mi, Zhang Hua, Liu Kun, and Pan Ni for honoring antiquity yet mingling with the vulgar stream without raising themselves—what Cao Zhi and Lu Ji could not attain;
translations.idiomatic: Yingshi often praised Ban Biao, Huangfu Mi, Zhang Hua, Liu Kun, and Pan Ni for honoring antiquity while still mingling with the vulgar world without elevating themselves—something Cao Zhi and Lu Ji never achieved;

sentences.zh: 又言裴子野善著書。

translations.literal: He also said that Pei Ziye was skilled at writing books.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that Pei Ziye was skilled at historical writing.

sentences.zh: 所許可當世者，陳子昂、富嘉謨、盧藏用之文辭，董南事、孔述睿之博學而已。

translations.literal: Those of his own age whom he approved were only the literary compositions of Chen Zi'ang, Fu Jiamou, and Lu Zangyong, and the broad learning of Dong Nanshi and Kong Shurui.
translations.idiomatic: Among his contemporaries he approved only the literary work of Chen Zi'ang, Fu Jiamou, and Lu Zangyong, and the erudition of Dong Nanshi and Kong Shurui.

sentences.zh: 子 存子存，字伯誠，亮直有父風。

translations.literal: His son Cun, courtesy name Bocheng, was upright and outspoken and had his father's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cun, whose courtesy name was Bocheng, was upright and outspoken and bore his father's character.

sentences.zh: 能文辭，與韓會、沈既濟、梁肅、徐岱等善。

translations.literal: He was skilled at literary composition and was on good terms with Han Hui, Shen Jiji, Liang Su, Xu Dai, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at literary composition and was close to Han Hui, Shen Jiji, Liang Su, Xu Dai, and others.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使李棲筠表常熟主簿。

translations.literal: Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of Zhexi, memorialized recommending him as chief clerk of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of Zhexi, recommended him for appointment as chief clerk of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 顏真卿在湖州，與存及陸鴻漸等討摭古今韻字所原，作書數百篇。

translations.literal: When Yan Zhenqing was in Huzhou, together with Cun and Lu Hongjian and others he collected and examined the origins of rhyming characters ancient and modern, composing several hundred chapters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: While Yan Zhenqing was in Huzhou, he worked with Cun, Lu Hongjian, and others to gather and examine the origins of rhyming characters through the ages, producing several hundred treatises.

sentences.zh: 建中初，由殿中侍御史四遷比部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, from Palace Censor he was promoted four times to Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, he rose from Palace Censor through four promotions to Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 張滂主財賦，辟存留務京師。

translations.literal: Zhang Pang was in charge of fiscal affairs and appointed Cun to remain at the capital to manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang, who oversaw fiscal affairs, appointed Cun to remain at the capital and manage administrative affairs there.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡與滂不協，存疾其奸，去官，風痹卒。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling did not get along with Pang; Cun detested Yanling's wickedness, left office, and died of rheumatism.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling was at odds with Pang. Cun loathed Yanling's corruption, resigned his post, and died of rheumatism.

sentences.zh: 韓愈少為存所知，自袁州還，過存廬山故居，而諸子前死，唯一女在，為經贍其家。

translations.literal: When Han Yu was young, Cun recognized his talent. Returning from Yuan Prefecture, he passed Cun's former residence on Mount Lu; Cun's sons had all died earlier, and only one daughter remained. Han Yu managed and provided for her household.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu had been recognized by Cun when he was young. Returning from Yuan Prefecture, he visited Cun's former home on Mount Lu. Cun's sons had all died earlier, leaving only a daughter, and Han Yu took charge of supporting her household.

sentences.zh: 殷寅者，陳郡人。

translations.literal: Yin Yin was a man of Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yin was from Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 邵軫者，汝南人。

translations.literal: Shao Zhen was a man of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Zhen was from Runan.

sentences.zh: 附 陸據陸據，河南人，字德鄰，後周上庸公騰六世孫。

translations.literal: Appended: Lu Ju—Lu Ju, a native of Henan, courtesy name Delin, was sixth-generation descendant of Duke Teng of Shangyong of Northern Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Lu Ju, a native of Henan whose courtesy name was Delin, was a sixth-generation descendant of Duke Teng of Shangyong of Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 神宇警邁，善物理。

translations.literal: His bearing was alert and lofty, and he was skilled at natural principles.
translations.idiomatic: He had an alert and commanding presence and was versed in natural philosophy.

sentences.zh: 年三十始到京師，公卿愛其文，交譽之。

translations.literal: Not until he was thirty did he first reach the capital; the nobles loved his writing and praised him to one another.
translations.idiomatic: He did not reach the capital until he was thirty, but the nobles admired his writing and praised him among themselves.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載，終司勳員外郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao, he died while serving as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Tianbao era, he died in office as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 附 柳並柳並者，字伯存。

translations.literal: Appended: Liu Bing—Liu Bing, courtesy name Bocun.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Liu Bing, whose courtesy name was Bocun.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，辟河東府掌書記，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, he was appointed secretary of the Hedong headquarters, then promoted to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era, he was appointed secretary at the Hedong headquarters and was later promoted to Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 喪明，終於家。

translations.literal: He lost his sight and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He went blind and died at home.

sentences.zh: 初，並與劉太真、尹征、閻士和受業於穎士，而並好黃老。

translations.literal: At first, Bing together with Liu Taizhen, Yin Zheng, and Yan Shihe studied under Yingshi, but Bing favored Huang-Lao thought.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Bing had studied under Yingshi together with Liu Taizhen, Yin Zheng, and Yan Shihe, but Bing favored Huang-Lao teachings.

sentences.zh: 穎士常曰：「太真，吾入室者也，斯文不墜，寄是子雲。

translations.literal: Yingshi often said: "Taizhen is my true disciple; if this tradition does not fall, it will rest with this Ziyun.
translations.idiomatic: Yingshi often said, "Taizhen is my true heir; if this literary tradition does not perish, it will rest with this Ziyun.

sentences.zh: 征博聞強識，士和鉤深致遠，吾弗逮已。

translations.literal: Zheng was broadly learned with a strong memory; Shihe probed deep and reached far—I cannot match them.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng is broadly learned with a formidable memory; Shihe probes deep and reaches far—I cannot match them.

sentences.zh: 並不受命而尚黃、老，予亦何誅？」

translations.literal: Bing did not accept my teaching yet honors Huang-Lao—what fault can I find in him?"
translations.idiomatic: Bing did not follow my teaching yet honors Huang-Lao—what reproach can I hold against him?"

sentences.zh: 並弟談，字中庸，穎士愛其才，以女妻之。

translations.literal: Bing's younger brother Tan, courtesy name Zhongyong, was loved by Yingshi for his talent, and Yingshi gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's younger brother Tan, whose courtesy name was Zhongyong, was admired by Yingshi for his talent, and Yingshi gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 士和字伯均，著《蘭陵先生誄》、《蕭夫子集論》，因榷曆世文章，而盛推穎士所長，以為「聞蕭氏風者，五尺童子羞稱曹、陸」。

translations.literal: Shihe, courtesy name Bojun, wrote the Elegy for Master Lanling and the Treatise on Master Xiao's Collected Works; by weighing literary works through the ages, he greatly praised Yingshi's strengths, saying that "those who have heard the style of the Xiao house are ashamed, even at five feet tall, to mention Cao and Lu."
translations.idiomatic: Shihe, whose courtesy name was Bojun, wrote the Elegy for Master Lanling and the Treatise on Master Xiao's Collected Works. Surveying literature through the ages, he greatly praised Yingshi's strengths, declaring that "those who have tasted the Xiao style would be ashamed—even a child of five feet—to mention Cao Zhi and Lu Ji."

sentences.zh: 附 皇甫冉皇甫冉，字茂政，十歲便能屬文，張九齡歎異之。

translations.literal: Appended: Huangfu Ran—Huangfu Ran, courtesy name Maozheng, could compose prose at ten; Zhang Jiujing marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Huangfu Ran, whose courtesy name was Maozheng, was composing prose by the age of ten, and Zhang Jiujing marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 與弟曾皆善詩。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Zeng were both skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Zeng were both accomplished poets.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，踵登進士，授無錫尉。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, both in succession passed the jinshi examination and were appointed magistrate of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, both brothers passed the jinshi examination in succession and were appointed magistrate of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 王縉為河南元帥，表掌書記。

translations.literal: Wang Jin was marshal of Henan and memorialized appointing him secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin, marshal of Henan, recommended him for appointment as secretary.

sentences.zh: 遷累右補闕，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Right Supplementation Censor and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Right Supplementation Censor and then died.

sentences.zh: 曾，字孝常，曆監察御史。

translations.literal: Zeng, courtesy name Xiaochang, served as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng, whose courtesy name was Xiaochang, served as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 其名與冉相上下，當時比張氏景陽、孟陽雲。

translations.literal: His fame ranked with Ran's; at the time they were compared to the Zhang brothers Jingyang and Mengyang.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation matched Ran's; at the time the two were compared to the Zhang brothers Jingyang and Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 蘇源明蘇源明，京兆武功人，初名預，字弱夫。

translations.literal: Su Yuanming—Su Yuanming, a native of Wugong in Jingzhao, originally named Yu, courtesy name Ruofu.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yuanming, a native of Wugong in Jingzhao whose original name was Yu and courtesy name was Ruofu.

sentences.zh: 少孤，寓居徐、兗。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he lived in Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he lived in Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 工文辭，有名天寶間。

translations.literal: He was skilled at literary composition and was famous in the Tianbao era.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at literary composition and won renown during the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，更試集賢院。

translations.literal: After passing the jinshi examination, he underwent further examination at the Collegiate Institute.
translations.idiomatic: After earning his jinshi degree, he underwent further examination at the Collegiate Institute.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子諭德。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 出為東平太守。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 是時，濟陽郡太守李倰以郡瀕河，請增領宿城、中都二縣以紓民力。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jun, prefect of Jiyang Commandery, because the commandery bordered the river, requested additionally to administer Sucheng and Zhongdu counties to relieve the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Jun, prefect of Jiyang Commandery, noting that his commandery bordered the Yellow River, requested additionally to administer Sucheng and Zhongdu counties in order to ease the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 二縣，隸東平、魯郡者也。

translations.literal: The two counties were under Dongping and Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Those two counties had belonged to Dongping and Lu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 於是源明議廢濟陽，析三縣分隸濟南、東平、濮陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuanming proposed abolishing Jiyang and dividing three counties to be placed under Jinan, Dongping, and Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming then proposed abolishing Jiyang and redistributing three counties among Jinan, Dongping, and Puyang.

sentences.zh: 詔河南採訪使會濮陽太守崔季重、魯郡太守李蘭、濟南太守田琦及源明、倰五太守議于東平，不能決。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Henan investigation commissioner to convene Cui Jizhong, prefect of Puyang, Li Lan, prefect of Lu Commandery, Tian Qi, prefect of Jinan, and the five prefects Yuanming and Jun to deliberate at Dongping, but they could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Henan investigation commissioner to convene Cui Jizhong, prefect of Puyang, Li Lan, prefect of Lu Commandery, Tian Qi, prefect of Jinan, and the five prefects Yuanming and Jun at Dongping for deliberation, but no decision could be reached.

sentences.zh: 既而卒廢濟陽，以縣皆隸東平。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jiyang was abolished in the end, and all the counties were placed under Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Jiyang was abolished, and all the counties were placed under Dongping.

sentences.zh: 召源明為國子司業。

translations.literal: Yuanming was summoned to serve as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming was summoned to serve as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 安祿山陷京師，源明以病不受偽署。

translations.literal: When An Lushan took the capital, Yuanming, citing illness, did not accept a false appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan seized the capital, Yuanming, pleading illness, refused a false appointment under the rebels.

sentences.zh: 肅宗復兩京，擢考功郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong recovered the two capitals, Yuanming was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel and entrusted with drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Suzong recovered the two capitals, Yuanming was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel and entrusted with drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 是時，承大盜之余，國用覂屈，宰相王璵以祈禬進，禁中禱祀窮日夜，中官用事，給養繁靡，群臣莫敢切諍。

translations.literal: At that time, inheriting the aftermath of great rebellion, the state's resources were exhausted; Chief Minister Wang Yu advanced through prayer rituals, and within the palace offerings and prayers continued day and night; eunuchs held power; provisions and upkeep were lavish and wasteful; no minister dared remonstrate sharply.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, in the wake of the great rebellion, the treasury was exhausted. Chief Minister Wang Yu rose through promoting prayer rituals, and within the palace offerings and prayers continued day and night. Eunuchs held power, provisions and upkeep were lavish and wasteful, and no minister dared speak out sharply.

sentences.zh: 昭應令梁鎮上書勸帝罷淫祀，其他不暇及也。

translations.literal: Liang Zhen, magistrate of Zhaoying, submitted a memorial urging the emperor to stop excessive sacrifices; other matters there was no time to reach.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhen, magistrate of Zhaoying, submitted a memorial urging the emperor to halt excessive sacrifices, but there was no time to address anything else.

sentences.zh: 源明數陳政治得失。

translations.literal: Yuanming repeatedly set forth the gains and losses of government.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming repeatedly set forth the strengths and failings of government policy.

sentences.zh: 及史思明陷洛陽，有詔幸東京，將親征。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming took Luoyang, there was an edict that the emperor would visit the Eastern Capital and personally campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming seized Luoyang, an edict was issued that the emperor would visit the Eastern Capital and take the field in person.

sentences.zh: 源明因上疏極諫曰：

translations.literal: Yuanming thereupon submitted a memorial remonstrating to the utmost, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming thereupon submitted a memorial of the strongest remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 淫雨積時，道路方梗，甚不可一也。

translations.literal: Prolonged excessive rain has accumulated for a long time, and the roads are now blocked—this is most inadvisable, first of all.
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged rains have gone on and on, and the roads are now impassable—this above all must not be done.

sentences.zh: 自春大旱，秋苗耗半，斂獲未畢，先之以清道之役，申之以供頓之苦，甚不可二也。

translations.literal: Since spring there has been great drought; half the autumn crops are lost; the harvest is not yet complete, yet first comes the labor of clearing the roads, followed by the hardship of supply depots—this is most inadvisable, second of all.
translations.idiomatic: Since spring there has been severe drought, and half the autumn crop is lost. The harvest is not yet in, yet first comes the labor of clearing the roads, and on top of that the hardship of supply depots—this, second of all, must not be done.

sentences.zh: 每立殿廊，見旌旗之下，餓夫執殳，僕於行間，日見二三；

translations.literal: Every time I stand in the palace corridor, beneath the banners and flags I see starving men holding halberds collapse among the ranks—two or three such cases each day;
translations.idiomatic: Each time I stand in the palace corridor, beneath the banners and flags I see starving men holding halberds collapse in the ranks—two or three such cases every day;

sentences.zh: 市井餒𩛞求食，死于路旁，日見四五。

translations.literal: in the markets the hungry seek food and die by the roadside—four or five such cases each day.
translations.idiomatic: in the markets the hungry wander seeking food and die by the roadside—four or five such cases every day.

sentences.zh: 甚不可三也。

translations.literal: This is most inadvisable, third of all.
translations.idiomatic: This, third of all, must not be done.

sentences.zh: 姦夫盜兒，連牆接棟，磨礪以須陛下之出，御史大夫必不能澄清禁止。

translations.literal: Adulterers and thieves stand wall to wall and wall to roof, sharpening their blades awaiting Your Majesty's departure—the Censor-in-Chief surely cannot purge and forbid them.
translations.idiomatic: Adulterers and thieves crowd wall to wall and roof to roof, sharpening their blades in wait for Your Majesty's departure—the Censor-in-Chief surely cannot purge and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 甚不可四也。

translations.literal: This is most inadvisable, fourth of all.
translations.idiomatic: This, fourth of all, must not be done.

sentences.zh: 聖皇巡蜀之初，都內財貨、吏民資產，糜散于道路之手，至有乘馬駃驢入宣政、紫宸者。

translations.literal: When the sage emperor first toured Shu, the capital's wealth and goods and officials' and people's property were scattered into the hands of those on the roads, until some rode horses and mules into the Xuanzheng and Zichen halls.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage emperor first fled to Shu, the capital's wealth and the property of officials and commoners were scattered into the hands of those on the roads, until some rode horses and mules straight into the Xuanzheng and Zichen halls.

sentences.zh: 況陛下初有四海，威制不及曩時遠矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty has only lately come into possession of all under Heaven; your authority falls far short of that time.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty has only lately regained the realm; your authority falls far short of what it was then.

sentences.zh: 今茲東行，殆賊臣誘掖陛下而已。

translations.literal: This eastern journey now is likely nothing but wicked ministers seducing and leading Your Majesty astray.
translations.idiomatic: This eastern journey now is likely nothing but wicked ministers seducing and misleading Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰「三星在霤」，謂危亡在於須臾，臣不勝嗚咽，為陛下痛之。

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says, "The three stars are in the leak"—meaning that peril and ruin lie within an instant. I cannot bear it and weep for Your Majesty in anguish.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry says, "The three stars are in the leak"—meaning that peril and ruin lie within an instant. I cannot bear it and weep in anguish for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 願速罷幸，不然，窮氓樂禍，已扼腕於下。

translations.literal: I beg that the tour be quickly cancelled; otherwise the destitute masses will welcome disaster, and already below they are clenching their fists.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the tour be cancelled at once; otherwise the destitute masses will welcome disaster, and already below they are clenching their fists in rage.

sentences.zh: 甚不可五也。

translations.literal: This is most inadvisable, fifth of all.
translations.idiomatic: This, fifth of all, must not be done.

sentences.zh: 方今河、洛驛騷，江湖叛渙，《詩》曰：「中原有菽，庶民采之。」

translations.literal: At present the Yellow River and Luo region are in turmoil, and the Jiang-Hu region is in rebellion and disarray. The Classic of Poetry says: "In the central plain there are beans; the common people gather them.
translations.idiomatic: At present the Yellow River and Luo region are in turmoil, and the Jiang-Hu region is in rebellion and disarray. The Classic of Poetry says: "In the central plain there are beans; the common people gather them.

sentences.zh: 彼思明、楚元，皆采菽之人也。

translations.literal: Those Siming and Chu Yuan are all bean-gatherers.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming and Chu Yuan are precisely such bean-gatherers.

sentences.zh: 陛下何遽輕萬乘而速成之邪？

translations.literal: Why should Your Majesty so hastily treat lightly the imperial chariot and rush to complete the journey?
translations.idiomatic: Why should Your Majesty so lightly risk the imperial chariot and rush to complete this journey?

sentences.zh: 甚不可六也。

translations.literal: This is most inadvisable, sixth of all.
translations.idiomatic: This, sixth of all, must not be done.

sentences.zh: 大河南北，舉為寇盜，王公以下，廩稍匱絕，將士糧賜，僅支日月，而中官冗食，不減往年，梨園雜伎，愈盛今日，陛下未得穆然高枕，殆繇此也。

translations.literal: North and south of the great river all have become bandits; from princes and dukes downward, granary stipends are exhausted; soldiers' grain and rewards barely last from day to day and month to month; yet the redundant eating of eunuchs is no less than in former years, and Pear Garden variety performers flourish even more today—Your Majesty cannot rest peacefully on a high pillow, likely because of this.
translations.idiomatic: North and south of the great river have all become bandit country. From princes and dukes downward, granary stipends are exhausted; soldiers' grain and rewards barely last from day to day. Yet eunuchs' redundant consumption is no less than in former years, and Pear Garden performers flourish even more today—Your Majesty cannot rest peacefully, likely for this very reason.

sentences.zh: 自非中庸指使，太常正樂外，願一切放歸，給長牒勿事，須五六年後，隨事蠲省。

translations.literal: Except for the directors of the Zhongyong Office and the proper music of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, I wish that all others be released and given long permits without duties; only after five or six years should reductions be made according to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the directors of the Zhongyong Office and the proper music of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, I wish that all others be dismissed and given long-term permits exempting them from service; only after five or six years should reductions be made as circumstances allow.

sentences.zh: 今聚而仰給，甚不可七也。

translations.literal: Now they are gathered and depend on state support—this is most inadvisable, seventh of all.
translations.idiomatic: Now they are gathered together living on state support—this, seventh of all, must not be done.

sentences.zh: 李光弼拔河陽，王思禮下晉原，衛伯玉拂焉耆，過析支，不日可至。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi has taken Heyang; Wang Sili has taken Jinyuan; Wei Boyu has swept Yanzhi and passed Qizhi—they can arrive within days.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi has recovered Heyang; Wang Sili has taken Jinyuan; Wei Boyu has swept through Yanzhi and passed Qizhi—they can arrive within days.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫王玄志壓巫閭，臨幽都；

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Xuanzhi presses Wulü and faces Youdu;
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Xuanzhi presses Wulü and faces Youdu;

sentences.zh: 汝州刺史田南金逾闕口，遏二室；

translations.literal: Tian Nanjin, prefect of Ruzhou, crosses Quekou and blocks the Two Chambers;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Nanjin, prefect of Ruzhou, crosses Quekou and blocks the Two Chambers;

sentences.zh: 鄧景山淩淮、泗，愾然而西。

translations.literal: Deng Jingshan crosses the Huai and Si and marches west in high spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jingshan crosses the Huai and Si and marches west in high spirits.

sentences.zh: 狂賊失勢，蹙於緱山之下，北不敢逾孟津，東不敢過甖子，計日反接而至矣。

translations.literal: The mad rebels have lost momentum and are cornered below Mount Goushan; they dare not north cross Mengjin or east pass Yingzi; within days they can be bound hand behind back and delivered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel forces have lost momentum and are cornered below Mount Goushan. They dare not cross Mengjin to the north or pass Yingzi to the east; within days they can be bound hand and foot and delivered up.

sentences.zh: 陛下不坐而受之，乃欲親征，徇一朝之怒，甚不可八也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty need not sit and receive them, yet wishes to campaign in person, indulging a morning's anger—this is most inadvisable, eighth of all.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty need only sit and receive their surrender, yet wishes to campaign in person, indulging a moment's anger—this, eighth of all, must not be done.

sentences.zh: 王者之於天地神祇，享之以牲幣而已。

translations.literal: A king toward the spirits of Heaven and Earth need only offer them sacrificial victims and silks.
translations.idiomatic: A king's duty toward the spirits of Heaven and Earth is to offer them sacrificial victims and silks—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 記曰：「不祈方士。」

translations.literal: The Record says: "Do not pray to masters of formulas.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says: "Do not pray to masters of formulas.

sentences.zh: 彼淫巫愚祝，妄有關說，甚不可九也。

translations.literal: Those licentious shamans and foolish prayer-officers presumptuously intercede—this is most inadvisable, ninth of all.
translations.idiomatic: Those licentious shamans and foolish prayer-officers presumptuously intercede on Heaven's behalf—this, ninth of all, must not be done.

sentences.zh: 天子順動，人皆幸之之謂幸，人皆病之之謂不幸。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven acts in accord with the people's wishes, if all rejoice it is called a tour of fortune; if all suffer it is called misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven acts in accord with the people's wishes, if all rejoice it is called a fortunate tour; if all suffer it is called an ill-fated one.

sentences.zh: 臣等屢怫視聽，聯伏赤墀之下，頓顙流涕而出，雖陛下優容貸罪，凡百之臣必昌言于朝，萬口謗於外，甚不可十也。

translations.literal: We have repeatedly offended Your Majesty's sight and hearing, bowing prostrate below the red steps and bowing our heads in tears as we withdrew. Even if Your Majesty is lenient and pardons our offense, every official will surely speak boldly at court, and ten thousand mouths will slander outside—this is most inadvisable, tenth of all.
translations.idiomatic: We have repeatedly offended Your Majesty's sight and hearing, prostrating ourselves below the red steps and bowing our heads in tears as we withdrew. Even if Your Majesty is lenient and pardons us, every official will surely speak boldly at court, and countless voices will slander outside—this, tenth of all, must not be done.

sentences.zh: 臣聞子不諍于父，不孝也；

translations.literal: I have heard that a son who does not remonstrate with his father is unfilial;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a son who does not remonstrate with his father is unfilial;

sentences.zh: 臣不諍於君，不忠也。

translations.literal: a minister who does not remonstrate with his lord is disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: a minister who does not remonstrate with his lord is disloyal.

sentences.zh: 不孝不忠，為苟榮冒祿，圈牢之物不若也。

translations.literal: Unfilial and disloyal, seeking glory while accepting salary—you are not even the equal of penned livestock.
translations.idiomatic: To be unfilial and disloyal yet seek glory while accepting salary is to be worse than penned livestock.

sentences.zh: 臣雖至賤，不能委身圈牢之中，將使樵夫指而笑之。

translations.literal: Though I am of the lowest rank, I cannot entrust myself to a pen; I would rather let woodcutters point and laugh at me.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am of the lowest rank, I cannot entrust myself to such a pen; I would rather be pointed at and laughed at by woodcutters.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其切直，遂罷東幸。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his directness and forthrightness and thereupon cancelled the eastern tour.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his directness and forthrightness and cancelled the eastern tour.

sentences.zh: 後以秘書少監卒。

translations.literal: Later he died while serving as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 源明雅善杜甫、鄭虔，其最稱者元結、梁肅。

translations.literal: Yuanming was on excellent terms with Du Fu and Zheng Qian; those he most praised were Yuan Jie and Liang Su.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming was on excellent terms with Du Fu and Zheng Qian; those he most admired were Yuan Jie and Liang Su.

sentences.zh: 附 梁肅肅，字敬之，一字寬中。

translations.literal: Appended: Liang Su—Su, courtesy name Jingzhi, also styled Kuanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Liang Su, whose courtesy name was Jingzhi and who also styled himself Kuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 隋刑部尚書毘五世孫，世居陸渾。

translations.literal: He was fifth-generation descendant of Pei, Minister of Justice of Sui, and his family had long lived in Lu Hun.
translations.idiomatic: He was a fifth-generation descendant of Pei, Minister of Justice of Sui, and his family had long resided in Lu Hun.

sentences.zh: 建中初，中文辭清麗科，擢太子校書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, he passed the examination in elegant and pure literary composition and was promoted to Proofreader of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, he passed the examination in elegant and pure literary composition and was promoted to Proofreader of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 蕭復薦其材，授右拾遺，脩史，以母羸老不赴。

translations.literal: Xiao Fu recommended his talent and appointed him Right Pick-up Reminder and historiographer, but because his mother was frail and aged he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fu recommended his talent and appointed him Right Pick-up Reminder and historiographer, but because his mother was frail and aged he did not take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 杜佑辟淮南掌書記，召為監察御史，轉右補闕、翰林學士、皇太子諸王侍讀。

translations.literal: Du You appointed him secretary of the Huainan headquarters; he was summoned as investigating censor, then transferred to Right Supplementation Censor, Hanlin Academician, and Reader to the Crown Prince and the imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: Du You appointed him secretary of the Huainan headquarters. He was summoned as investigating censor, then transferred to Right Supplementation Censor, Hanlin Academician, and Reader to the Crown Prince and the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十一，贈禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He died at the age of forty-one, and posthumously received the title of Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-one and was posthumously appointed director in the Ministry of Rites.
